items.title: P2: wire the cross-repo boundary detector into make verify (offline snapshot body + quarantine baseline)
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
## Why

PR #387 (merge `de5b7ed`) landed the cross-repo execution boundary as a contract
plus a real detector (`governance/board/boundary.py`) with a fixture validated
against the live board. The detector is **not yet wired into `make verify`**, so
today the rule is enforced only when someone runs it — and GR-29 says a rule
that is not platform-enforced is advisory.

## Measured blockers to wiring (both real)

1. **The committed board snapshot carries no `body`.** `.board/snapshot.json`
   exports `number, title, state, labels, milestone, parent, blocked_by,
   closed_at` — no `body`. The detector reads the `## Repo` declaration from the
   body. Run against that export it returns `OK` on a board that genuinely holds
   11 cross-repo children — a **false green by missing field**. (This exact
   shape was caught and is now pinned by a test: a missing `state` is treated as
   open, fail-closed — but a missing `body` still means the check cannot assess.)
2. **No quarantine baseline exists for the legacy 11.** Running the detector on
   the real board today yields `NOT-OK — 11 boundary violation(s)` (children
   #126–#129, #131–#137). Wiring that into `make verify` unbaselined would turn
   the gate permanently red for every lane — the opposite of a useful signal.

## Required pattern (repo precedent: `governance/lifecycle/baseline.json`)

- Extend the board export (or add a boundary-specific export) so it carries
  `body`, regenerated by a documented code-native command (no GitHub Actions,
  GR-15).
- Add a `governance/board/boundary-baseline.json` that quarantines the 11 legacy
  children **by name**, honoured *only while the issue tracking it is open*, so
  the quarantine can only shrink — a **new** cross-repo item filed on this board
  must fail immediately.
- Wire a `scripts/check-cross-repo-boundary.sh` into `verify.sh`'s check list,
  with the repo's tri-state contract (0 OK / 1 NOT-OK / 2 CANNOT-ASSESS —
  CANNOT-ASSESS never a pass) and a **provoked negative control**: the script
  must prove it can fail, per `scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh`'s pattern.
- Mutation-prove the check: disable the declaration detector, expect red, restore
  byte-identical.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `make verify` includes the boundary check and is green on `master`.
- [ ] A newly filed issue declaring a foreign repo fails the gate (provoked).
- [ ] A quarantined legacy child passes while its tracker is open, and the
      quarantine entry becomes a stale finding once the tracker closes.
- [ ] Missing `body` in the snapshot is CANNOT-ASSESS, never OK.

Verify: `bash scripts/check-cross-repo-boundary.sh` and `make verify`

Refs: #125, #387, `docs/CROSS-REPO-EXECUTION-BOUNDARY.md`,
`governance/lifecycle/baseline.json` (precedent).

items.title: Cross-reference spine: typed relationships + cmr-refs marker convention, enforced (EPIC #138 DoD gap)
items.body:
Parent: #138

## GOAL

Build the **cross-reference spine** that EPIC #138 is named for: typed relationship edges in
the institutional knowledge index, a **`cmr-refs` marker convention** that is *enforced and
validated* (not advisory), and RCA objects as **first-class nodes** with `caused-by` /
`mitigates` relationships — then gate all of it so a broken cross-reference or a dead
`cmr-refs` target is a conformance failure, never a silent skip. Success = the catalog carries
a deterministic `relationships` list, the gate passes on the committed tree **and** fails when
a target is mutated, and `make verify` is green.

## Constraints

- One lane owns `governance/knowledge/`, the new gate script, and the gate wiring. Touch only
  your lane's files; do not reformat `Makefile`/`scripts/verify.sh` beyond your insertion.
- Cross-reference **generation is deterministic and reproducible**: no timestamps in the edge
  list, edges sorted, byte-stable across rebuilds.
- Do not seed `cmr-refs:` markers into files another lane owns (e.g. `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md`,
  the ADR index). Seed them only in files this lane owns.
- Every markdown link you add must resolve; `vendor/` paths in backticks only.

## Context

EPIC #138 (M24) children #139–#143 delivered the index **nodes** (`governance/knowledge/`:
`model.py` `KnowledgeItem` = id/kind/path/title/provenance/tags/keywords; `catalog.json` top
keys = counts/coverage/findings/generated_at/item_count/items/repo/schema — **no relationships
key**), provenance, secret policy, conformance, lessons, remediation and the board gate. The
**edges** were never built. The raw data to turn into edges already exists in-repo:

- ADR front-matter `supersedes:` (e.g. ADR-0012) → `supersedes` edges.
- `.board/snapshot.json` issue `Parent:`/`Blocked-by:` → `parent-of` / `blocked-by` edges.
- `governance/lessons/ledger.jsonl` — records of kind `incident`/`rca`/`corrective-action`/
  `lesson`, with fields `origin`, `incident`, `rca`, `corrective_actions`, `artifact` →
  `caused-by` (rca→incident), `mitigates` (corrective-action→rca, lesson→incident), `origin`
  (rca/incident→issue|pr|commit).
- `governance/lessons/rca/RCA-*.md` — the RCA artifacts (already carry the required sections).
- `cmr-refs:` markers in tracked markdown → `refs` edges (this lane defines the marker syntax
  and validates every target exists).

## Deliverables (files this lane owns)

1. `governance/knowledge/model.py` — add a `Relationship` dataclass (from_id, type, to_id,
   optional `via`) and a **closed** relationship vocabulary, e.g.
   `supersedes | parent-of | blocked-by | caused-by | mitigates | origin | refs | part-of |
   implements`; add `relationships` to `Index.as_dict()` / `from_dict()`.
2. `governance/knowledge/crossref.py` (new) — deterministic builder: reads the ADR front-matter,
   `.board/snapshot.json`, `governance/lessons/ledger.jsonl` and tracked-`cmr-refs:` markers,
   emits a **sorted, deduplicated** edge list.
3. `governance/knowledge/indexer.py` — call the crossref builder during build so the catalogue
   carries `relationships`.
4. `governance/knowledge/catalog.json` — **regenerated** with the new `relationships` key
   (build twice and assert byte-identical to prove determinism).
5. `governance/knowledge/README.md` — document the `cmr-refs:` marker syntax and the closed
   relationship vocabulary.
6. `docs/CROSS-REFERENCE-SPINE.md` (new) — the normative convention doc (marker syntax, where
   it is valid, what a valid target is, the vocabulary, and the no-silent-skip rule).
7. `scripts/check-cross-reference.sh` (new, `chmod +x`) — the gate; see below.
8. `Makefile` + `scripts/verify.sh` — wire the gate (`cross-reference` check) into the gate of
   record; insert `scripts/verify.sh`'s entry immediately AFTER the `'knowledge-index|…'` line.
9. `docs/README.md` — one row for `docs/CROSS-REFERENCE-SPINE.md`.

## The `cmr-refs:` convention (define and enforce exactly this)

- A marker is a markdown line matching `cmr-refs:` followed by a comma-separated list of
  targets. Target forms: `ADR-NNNN`, `GR-N`, `#N` (issue), `RCA-NNNN`, `LESSON-NNNN`, `INC-NNNN`,
  or a repo-relative path in backticks.
- The gate must: parse every marker in tracked `.md` files (outside `vendor/`, `.research/`,
  `.git/`), reject malformed markers (bad syntax, unknown kind prefix), and **reject any target
  that does not resolve** (file exists, or entity id present in the catalogue / board snapshot /
  ledger). A `cmr-refs:` target that cannot be validated is a FAIL, never a skip.

## The gate `scripts/check-cross-reference.sh`

Follow the repo gate style (`scripts/check-knowledge-index.sh`, `scripts/check-fleet-contract.sh`):
bash, `set -u`, `root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"`, tri-state exit
`0 OK / 1 NOT-OK / 2 CANNOT-ASSESS`, and a **negative control that mutates its own input**.
It must FAIL (exit 1) naming the file and the missing thing when:

- the catalogue is missing the `relationships` key, or an edge uses a type outside the closed
  vocabulary, or an edge endpoint does not resolve;
- a `cmr-refs:` marker is malformed, or names a target that does not resolve (dead reference);
- the determinism assertion fails (two builds differ).

Negative control: copy the convention doc to a temp dir, change one `cmr-refs:` target to a
bogus id, assert the text changed (`assert mutated != original`) and the sha256 differs, and
require the gate to refuse it. If the mutant passes, print FAIL and exit non-zero. Exit 2 only
when it cannot assess. Temp dirs: `mkdir "/tmp/ao138x.$$.$(date +%s)"` — never three consecutive
X (the repo's docs-lint rejects `XXX` in `.sh`).

## House rules that WILL fail the gate if you break them

- `bash -n` on every `.sh`; every `.py` compiles (`python3 -m py_compile`); every `.json`
  parses; no trailing whitespace in `.md`/`.sh`/`.py`/`.yaml`/`Makefile`; no
  `TODO`/`FIXME`/`HACK`/`XXX` word-boundary markers in `.sh`/`.py`; every relative markdown link
  resolves; `pytest governance/knowledge/tests` and `pytest governance/lessons/tests` stay green.

## Verification (run in your lane worktree; cwd-independent — use absolute paths)

```
bash -n scripts/check-cross-reference.sh
python3 -m py_compile governance/knowledge/crossref.py governance/knowledge/model.py governance/knowledge/indexer.py
python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py build && python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py build   # determinism: identical
bash scripts/check-knowledge-index.sh
bash scripts/check-cross-reference.sh
python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q governance/knowledge/tests governance/lessons/tests
bash scripts/check-docs.sh
```

Redirect ALL output to a uniquely named /tmp log and read it back with the file reader (the
shared terminal interleaves other lanes' output; a sibling's Ctrl-C can kill a run — detach with
`setsid` or re-run). Do NOT run `make verify` (the orchestrator runs it once per lane).

**Mutation proof you must capture:** gate rc 0 on your tree → break a `cmr-refs:` target →
confirm rc != 0 with a message naming the file + missing target → restore → confirm sha256
matches the original. Also run the built-in negative control. Report exact commands and real
output.

## Commit

```
git -C <worktree> add <explicit file list — never -A>
git -C <worktree> -c user.name=agent-copilot-crossref -c user.email=agent+copilot-crossref@agents.invalid commit -F <message-file>
```

Subject ends with `(#<issue>)`; body carries the literal trailer
`Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<issue>`. If `.board/snapshot.json` is modified, `git -C
<worktree> checkout -- .board/snapshot.json` BEFORE committing — never stage it. Leave
`vendor/CMR` alone. Do NOT push.

## Report back (concise, factual)

1. The relationship vocabulary and the exact edge counts by type you generated.
2. The `cmr-refs:` marker syntax you defined and where you seeded it.
3. Files created/modified with line counts; whether `catalog.json` regenerated byte-identically.
4. The gate's assertions + the exact mutation-proof transcript (commands, real rc, messages,
   before/after sha256).
5. Exact output of every check above.
6. Commit sha + `git show --stat`.
7. Anything not completed, and why.
Never claim a check passed unless you ran it and can quote its output.

items.title: Board hygiene: give every open issue its epic Parent: edge (attribution sweep)
items.body:
# Board hygiene: give every open issue its epic `Parent:` edge (attribution sweep)

> **Type:** board/PMO hygiene — GitHub board metadata only; no code, no repo files.
> **Owner-authorised** 2026-09-13 ("update all github issues without epics into
> epics they belong to"). This executes the **orphan dispositions of #358**
> ("Board attack plan", the current plan of record) for the *epic relation*.

## Problem (measured on the live board, 2026-09-13)

The repo's epic relation of record is the `Parent: #n` body marker — parsed by
`governance/dispatch/snapshot.py` into `.board/snapshot.json`, consumed by the
claim gate (`child-of-claim`) and by epic close-out. Measured live:

- 222 issues, 55 open; 12 carry `type:epic` (4 open: #138 #144 #160 #338).
- **35 open issues declared no `Parent:` edge at all** — including all six M25
  children (#145–#151) whose epic #144 names them in its own body, and two
  EPIC-titled issues (#125, #360) carrying **no `type:epic` label**, so the gate
  treated them as ordinary claimable work.

## Rules applied

1. **Open issues only** — closed history is never rewritten (decision 3).
2. **One parent per issue** — never multiply-parent; first `Parent:` wins in the parser.
3. **The target must be a labelled epic** — where an issue is an epic by title but
   not by label, `type:epic` is added first (#125, #359, #360).
4. **An edge needs evidence** — the owning epic's own body/manifest, or the class
   mapping recorded in #358 §4. Nothing is guessed from title similarity alone.
5. **Named exemptions** — cross-cutting PMO artifacts that belong to no epic are
   exempt **by name**: #329 (superseded plan), #358 (current plan), and this issue.

## Sweep (29 edges + 3 labels)

| Epic | Issues attached | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **#125** vendor-compliance | #126 #127 #128 #129 #131 #132 #133 #134 #135 #136 #137 | per-repo gaps in #125's own backlog |
| **#144** (M25) | #145 #146 #147 #149 #150 #151 | #144's body names all six as its children |
| **#160** (M26) | #174 #218 #241 #286 #287 #309 #360 #366 #367 | fleet runtime/governance surfaces (#358 §4) |
| **#360** (second-fleet UX epic, now labelled) | #365 | #365's body: "unblocks a second fleet …" |
| **#338** (SPoG) | #337 | #358 §4: fold into #349 (a #338 child) |

Labels: `type:epic` → **#125**, **#359**, **#360**. Unchanged: closed issues;
#138/#144/#160/#338 remain the milestone roots.

## Verify

- Every open issue either reaches a `type:epic` ancestor via its `Parent:` chain,
  or is a named exemption (the check is closed-world, so a new orphan fails it).
- Epic census after the sweep (`children_of()` per epic, from a fresh
  `cli.py snapshot --from-github` refresh in a scratch worktree).

Evidence is pasted in the comments below: exact commands + real output.

items.title: P0: hermes/paperclip/ollama unreachable — no shared-services fallback rung; a local-provider outage is a deal-breaker instead of a bounded degradation
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
## Symptom

When the **local** provider rungs — `hermes`, `paperclip`, `ollama` — are
unreachable (not running, not deployed, or crash-looping), the platform has **no
fallback rung**: the last hop of every routing chain is local Ollama, and when
that is down the chain reports *no healthy route* and the caller fails. Nothing
degrades onto the shared platform that already hosts these services. A single
local-provider outage is therefore a **deal-breaker / total outage**, and in the
fleet it is a crash-loop trigger (see #366).

## Evidence (measured on `master`)

- `gateway/providers/config.py` — every provider's fallback chain is
  `("ollama",)`, i.e. the **single local terminal rung**. `ollama` →
  `http://localhost:11434` (`requires_key=False`); `hermes` →
  `http://localhost:8080/api/chat` (model `hermes3`); `paperclip` →
  `https://api.paperclip.dev/v1`.
- `gateway/health/fallback.py` — `ChainRegistry.resolve()` returns `None` when
  even the local rung is unhealthy; the docstring states the caller "can escalate
  rather than silently send traffic to a dead model". There is **no rung after
  local Ollama**.
- `e2e/wiring.py` — `ENDPOINTS` hardcode `ollama=localhost:11434`,
  `paperclip=localhost:11435`, `hermes=localhost:11436`; `config.py`'s paperclip
  URL is `api.paperclip.dev` — the "paperclip" endpoint is **not even internally
  consistent** between the two composition roots.
- `module.json` — `distribution` declares python only; **no** compose/terraform
  in-repo hosts these services, so on any host that is not the dev laptop the
  `localhost` endpoints simply do not exist.
- **The shared layer already exists and is not consumed:** `kushin77/shared-services`
  (private, actively pushed) ships `services/model-server/`, `services/mcp-hub/`,
  `agents/ollama/`, `config/service-env/ollama.yaml`, `infra/docker-compose-prod.yml`,
  `docs/runbooks/ollama.md`. This repo references shared-services **only** as a
  cannibalization *source* (`docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` §22) — never as a runtime
  fallback.

## Gap

`localhost` is an **assumption**, not a deployment. When `hermes` / `paperclip` /
`ollama` are unreachable the platform should consume the **shared-services**
layer (model-server / ollama / MCP-hub) as the next rung — a *remote shared*
terminal hop — instead of failing hard. Today no such rung exists, so one local
outage is a total outage. This must not be a deal-breaker: it needs explicit
guardrails and a bounded blast radius.

## Guardrails required (make a local outage survivable)

1. **Explicit shared-services rung.** Add it to the degradation chain *after*
   local Ollama and *before* "no healthy route":
   `primary → … → local ollama → shared-services/<provider>`, resolved from a
   declared config (env / secret-manager endpoint) — **never a hardcoded URL**.
2. **Degrade, never crash.** An unreachable provider is a transient
   `ProviderUnavailableError` handled by the existing circuit breaker
   (`gateway/providers/resilience.py`), and the **fleet loop must treat it as a
   degraded result** — not as an exception that kills the sister rung and triggers
   the #366 crash-loop deadlock.
3. **Bounded retry + explicit refusal.** Retry/backoff is bounded; when *every*
   rung (local **and** shared) is unhealthy, the outcome is an **explicit**
   `denied` / `degraded` with a named reason — never a silent success, never an
   unbounded re-dispatch.
4. **Reachability is a health signal, not a crash.** A periodic reachability
   probe marks a rung unhealthy *before* traffic is sent; recovery is automatic
   (breaker `HALF_OPEN`), with no restart required.

## Blast radius (bounded by contract)

- **Blast radius = the single dispatch that needed the dead rung.** A dead local
  provider degrades *that call* to the shared rung (or refuses it); it must not
  wedge the claim, the directive, or the loop.
- **Never:** global halt, unbounded re-dispatch, silent success, or a
  claim/directive left consumed-but-unreported.
- **Contained units:** one provider rung → one degraded call → one report. The
  brain / sister rung stays live and idle-waiting (ties to #366 acceptance).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A declared shared-services rung exists (config + adapter), reachable when
      the local rung is down; **no hardcoded host**.
- [ ] Local provider unreachable → the call degrades to the shared rung, or
      refuses explicitly with a named reason; **the loop does not crash**.
- [ ] All rungs unhealthy → explicit degraded/denied; no silent success.
- [ ] A dead local rung cannot re-dispatch a directive more than once
      (mutation-proved; ties to #366).

Verify: `python3 -m pytest gateway/providers -q` **and** `python3 -m pytest gateway/health -q` (run per-suite: the two suites collide on a duplicate `test_events.py` basename when combined; `make verify` runs each in isolation)

Refs: #366 (crash-loop deadlock), #337 (unreachable team pins), #338 (six-agent
SPoG), #368 / #370 (paperclip seam), `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` §22.

items.title: Decision: embed-vs-fork-vs-CLI for paperclip.ing + freeze the integration seam (heartbeat/ticket/budget contracts)
items.body:
## GOAL

Decide **embed-vs-fork vs adopting the CLI** (`npx paperclipai`) as the operator surface,
record it as **ADR-0013**, and freeze the **integration seam** — heartbeat, ticket and
budget contracts — as machine-readable schemas plus a normative doc, all gated. Success =
the ADR is indexed, the three contracts exist and parse, and
`scripts/check-paperclip-integration.sh` passes on the committed tree **and** fails when the
decision or a contract is mutated.

## Constraints

- **Decide, don't re-open.** The decision is *which integration mode*; EPIC #359 already
  decided *whether* to adopt paperclip.ing.
- A contract that nothing validates is advisory (GR-29): each seam contract ships as a
  JSON Schema that parses **and** is named by the gate.
- ADR front-matter is required on a real ADR (`id`, `status`, `date`, `deciders`, `req`);
  reserved placeholders must not be fabricated into decisions.
- Do not edit `docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` (another lane owns it) or `vendor/`.

## Context

Upstream paperclip.ing exposes `/api` (company-scoped `/api/companies/{companyId}/...`,
board-token or agent-key/JWT auth, `X-Paperclip-Run-Id`, `/api/health`, `/api/openapi.json`)
and models work as org chart / goals / heartbeats / budgets / tickets+audit / governance.
The fleet already has the same verbs with different shapes: rung heartbeats
(`.fleet/*.heartbeat.json`), the claim ledger + `.fleet/slog.jsonl` + channel envelopes
(directive/ack/result/halt), and FinOps tiers + `telemetry/budgets` + `gateway/finops`.

Role: subagent
Epic: #359
Pillar: autonomous-ops
Lane: paperclip-integration
Model tier: pro
Thinking effort: medium
Verify command: make verify

Chain markers:

```
Parent: #359
Part-of: #359
Blocked-by: none
```

> Tier note: `pro` — this is an architecture decision with a frozen contract, not a
> mechanical edit (FinOps: escalate on the decision class, recorded here, not pre-emptive).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/decision-records/ADR-0013-paperclip-ing-integration.md` exists with required
      front-matter, `status: accepted`, and sections Status / Context / Decision /
      Consequences; the Decision names one of embed / fork / CLI-adopt and states the
      rejected alternatives and why (asserted by the gate)
- [ ] the ADR row exists in `docs/decision-records/README.md` with status `accepted`
      (asserted by the gate)
- [ ] `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-INTEGRATION.md` defines the seam: heartbeat, ticket and budget
      contracts, each with the fleet-side producer/consumer **file path** and the upstream
      surface it maps to (asserted by the gate)
- [ ] `docs/contracts/paperclip/{heartbeat,ticket,budget}.schema.json` exist, parse as JSON
      Schema, and declare the required fields the doc names (asserted by the gate)
- [ ] `scripts/check-paperclip-integration.sh` exits 0 on the committed tree and non-zero
      when the ADR's decision section is mutated (**mutation proof**, quoted)
- [ ] `make verify` PASS, quoted from `.verify/attestation.json`

## Evidence

```

```

items.title: Repoint the SPoG milestone (#338-#351, #331/#332/#333) at a paperclip.ing fork/embed
items.body:
## GOAL

Repoint the SPoG milestone at a **paperclip.ing fork/embed** instead of a from-scratch web
dashboard. Success = `docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` carries a repoint section that
names the superseding decision and what it supersedes, and the board records the repoint —
one append-only comment each on EPIC #338 and on #331/#332/#333 — with `make verify` green.

## Constraints

- **Record, do not commandeer.** Do not close, relabel, re-milestone or reassign #331,
  #332, #333 or #338–#351: ownership stays with their authors. The repoint is recorded in
  a comment and a doc section, nothing else.
- Append-only: no edits to any existing issue body.
- Do not edit `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md`, the ADR index, or `scripts/` — other lanes own those.

## Context

EPIC #359 decides the `ai.purebliss.app` management UI is a paperclip.ing fork/embed, not a
greenfield dashboard. `docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` is the document that framed the
gap and linked the roadmap (#331/#332/#333, plus the milestone "Agent Single Pane of Glass
(e2e)" = #338–#351); it must now carry the repoint so nobody builds the dashboard twice.

Role: subagent
Epic: #359
Pillar: control-plane
Lane: control-plane
Model tier: flash
Thinking effort: low
Verify command: make verify

Chain markers:

```
Parent: #359
Part-of: #359
Blocked-by: none
```

- [ ] `docs/FLEET-DASHBOARD-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` has a **Repointed** section that names the
      superseding decision, links the gap analysis and the ADR, and states explicitly what
      is *not* built any more (the from-scratch dashboard) and what is *not* affected (the
      terminal TUI stays)
- [ ] every markdown link in the amended doc resolves (`make docs-lint` green)
- [ ] a comment is posted on **#338** recording the repoint, naming this issue and the
      superseding decision, and linking the two docs
- [ ] a comment is posted on each of **#331**, **#332**, **#333** recording the repoint
- [ ] all four comments verified present (`gh api .../issues/<n>/comments` shows them) and
      quoted in the evidence

```

```

items.title: Paperclip.ing gap analysis — fleet primitives vs the reference agent-management product (provenance GR-10)
items.body:
## GOAL

Ship `docs/PAPERCLIP-ING-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` — a sourced, file-level gap analysis of
**paperclip.ing** (MIT, `github.com/paperclipai/paperclip`) against this fleet's own
primitives, with a **cannibalize-vs-build** table and **GR-10 provenance** — and gate it.
Success = the doc exists, the harvest is registered in the cannibalization index, and
`scripts/check-paperclip-gap-analysis.sh` passes on the committed tree **and** fails when
its provenance / namesake declarations are mutated.

## Constraints

- **Patterns, not code.** This is a fork-map/decision artifact, not a vendoring: cite the
  upstream product and its documented contracts; copy no source.
- Never edit `vendor/`; cite `vendor/` paths in backticks, never as markdown links
  (a fresh worktree has no `vendor/` contents, so a link fails `docs-lint`).
- Keep the four distinct "paperclips" separated: the fleet **agent** `paperclip`, the
  gateway **provider** `paperclip`, the vendored CMR **planning module** `paperclip`, and
  the upstream **product** paperclip.ing (see ADR-0012 for the first two).

## Context

EPIC #359 adopts paperclip.ing as the `ai.purebliss.app` agent-management surface rather
than building a web dashboard from scratch (#331/#332/#333, #338–#351). Upstream ships six
capability families: org chart, goal alignment, heartbeats, budgets/costs, tickets + audit,
governance. The fleet already ships a hand-built subset of each — this issue maps them.

Role: subagent

items.title: Wire live agent logs, KB access and mid-run steering over the A2A transport (non-stop live debug)
items.body:
Parent: #160

## Problem
The A2A transport exists (ADR-0011 + fleet/channel.py) but is a file-mailbox of *discrete* messages (directive/ack/result/escalate). It cannot carry (a) LIVE agent logs, (b) KB access, or (c) mid-run steering — so live debugging is poll-and-restart instead of continuous self-correction.

## Goal
Use the existing A2A transport for continuous, non-stop live debug until green:
1. **Live agent logs** — each subagent's stdout/events streamed over the channel (per-directive log stream + a `follow`/`listen --directive <id>` that tails it live).
2. **KB access** — a `kb` verb/query against the knowledge index (governance/knowledge/) so a running agent can pull the KB/lessons it needs instead of only the static paths attached to the directive.
3. **Mid-run steering** — a `steer` message the running loop/subagent honours mid-run (inject a hint/correction into a live run), so the brain can steer a stuck debug without killing and re-dispatching.

## Constraints
- Keep GR-21: localhost, file-based, no network daemons (so "live" = short-poll/long-poll over the mailbox, not a socket service).
- Preserve the existing contract (fleet/CONTRACT.md, ADR-0011) and the claim/release + run-marker invariants; add the verbs without weakening validation.

## Files
fleet/channel.py, fleet/terminal.py, fleet/brain.py, governance/knowledge/**, fleet/tests/**

## Verify
- `pytest fleet/tests -q` — new tests: log stream captured per directive; `steer` reaches a running run (negative control: without it the run does not change); KB query returns the index record.
- Live: steer a running directive and observe the run honour it without a re-dispatch.

items.title: P0: Fleet crash-loop / code-drift DEADLOCK — watchdog never respawns a drifted crash-looping loop, and a crashed run re-dispatches its directive forever
items.body:
Parent: #160

## Symptom

The fleet became untrustworthy: a **crash-loop / code-drift DEADLOCK**. The sister
rung ran stale code while HEAD advanced, every work directive crashed it in
seconds, and the watchdog never respawned it — so the loop stayed on broken code
forever while the same directives were re-dispatched indefinitely.

## Evidence (reproduced live from `.fleet/`)

**(a) The watchdog drift-vs-run-in-flight deadlock.**

`fleet/watchdog.py` `rung_action()` has one escape hatch:

```python
if state == "drifted" and name == "sister" and run_in_flight():
    return f"{name}: drifted ({reason}) but a run is in flight — left alone"
```

`.fleet/watchdog.log` shows this firing on every tick from 21:32 onward while the
brain — in the *same tick* — was respawned and picked up new code:

```
[watchdog] brain: drifted (running 37da4d6, HEAD eee23c5) — respawned
[watchdog] sister: drifted (running 37da4d6, HEAD eee23c5) but a run is in flight — left alone
[watchdog] sister: drifted (running 37da4d6, HEAD 592b132) but a run is in flight — left alone
...
[watchdog] brain: drifted (running eee23c5, HEAD 592b132) — respawned
```

`run_in_flight()` returns True on a run marker whose `pid` (the **loop's** pid,
`terminal.py:mark_run`) is alive — it never checks whether the run has a live
*child* or a fresh beat. A crashed run therefore leaves a marker that reads as
"a run in flight" for as long as the loop lives. Measured at RCA time,
`.fleet/runs/487c3aa7-….json` carried `"child_pid": null` and a stale `ts` but
`pid` = the live sister pid, so `run_in_flight()` was True with nothing running.
The guard protects *progress*; it has no crash-loop detector, so a run that never
completes and never progresses holds the drift lock open forever.

**(b) Infinite re-dispatch of an unconsumed directive after a crashed run.**

The old code ran the directive synchronously inside `loop()`, so the #310 bug
(`UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'verdict'`) killed the whole
sister process on every directive — 69 tracebacks in `.fleet/sister.log`. A
directive is only consumed on report (`channel.consume_directive`, called from
`cmd_report`), and a crashed run never reports. The next loop finds its own dead
claim (`held_action(...) → "self-heal"`) and **reaps and re-dispatches in the same
cycle** with no attempt counter and no backoff:

```
[terminal] #234 orphaned by our own dead run — reaping and re-dispatching
```

Measured churn in `.board/claims/` (claim → reap/release → re-claim, ~20–30s):

```
#341: 19 claims / 18 releases     #342: 17 / 17
#345: 16 / 16                     #350: 16 / 16
2026-09-14T01:42:45Z claim
2026-09-14T01:43:08Z release
2026-09-14T01:43:10Z claim
2026-09-14T01:43:31Z release
```

12 directives were left unconsumed in `.fleet/inbox`, so the loop re-read and
re-executed each one on every cycle.

## Fix (systemic, in code)

1. **Watchdog crash-loop escape.** A run is genuinely in flight only when its
   marker has a live child or a *fresh* beat; and a rung that is drifted **and**
   crash-looping (N respawns within a window, with no progress) is respawned even
   while a run appears in flight.
2. **At-most-once dispatch.** The run path records a persisted per-directive
   attempt count; a directive whose run keeps dying is backed off (not
   re-dispatched) instead of being retried every cycle.
3. **Brain-side guard.** The brain refuses to re-issue a directive for an issue
   that already has a live claim.

## Acceptance

- drifted + crash-looping → respawned (mutation-proved).
- a crashed run does not re-dispatch the same directive N times (mutation-proved).
- after merge + redeploy the running fleet is on the new commit.
- #341/#342/#345/#350 progress or fail for a REAL reason, not a crash loop.

Verify: `python3 -m pytest fleet/tests/test_watchdog.py fleet/tests/test_terminal.py fleet/tests/test_brain.py -q`

Refs: incident 2026-09-13/14, fleet rungs `brain → sister`.

## Goal
Make the fleet runtime namespaced so MULTIPLE fleets (brain+sister+monitor) can run on one machine without colliding. Unblocks a second fleet dedicated to the session-experience / portal / paperclip class.

## Scope

items.title: EPIC: Adopt paperclip.ing (MIT) as the ai.purebliss.app agent-management surface — fork/cannibalize, don't rebuild
items.body:
## Decision context
- paperclip.ing (https://paperclip.ing, github.com/paperclipai/paperclip, **MIT license**, self-hostable `npx paperclipai onboard`) is the reference agent-management product: org chart, heartbeats, goal alignment (mission→project→agent→task), per-agent budgets with hard limits, a ticket system with full tool-call tracing + immutable audit log, and governance (approve hires, override strategy, pause/resume/terminate). It is model-agnostic and supports Hermes/OpenClaw/Claude/Codex/etc.
- **Namesake warning:** this is NOT the vendored `paperclip` planning module (`vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/paperclip`) and NOT the gateway `paperclip` provider. Three distinct "paperclip"s; record provenance for each.
- Our fleet (brain/sister/subagents, heartbeats, claim ledger, FinOps tiers, escalate, waves, budgets, ticket trail) is a hand-built subset of what Paperclip already ships as a product.

## Decision
Fork/cannibalize paperclip.ing for the ai.purebliss.app agent-management UI (the "single pane of glass" from #313 / #331–#333), instead of building our own web dashboard from scratch. Map our existing primitives onto Paperclip's vocabulary: org chart ← SME profiles/personas; heartbeats ← rung heartbeats; goals/tasks ← EPIC→issue→micro-task waves; budgets ← FinOps tiers/limits; tickets ← directives + slog trail; governance ← controls (pause/stop/kill/override).

## Children
- Gap analysis: paperclip.ing features vs our fleet primitives, with a cannibalize-vs-build table and provenance (GR-10, cannibalization index #8).
- Repoint the SPoG milestone (#338–#351, #331/#332/#333) at a paperclip.ing fork/embed instead of a from-scratch web dashboard.
- Decide embed-vs-fork vs adopting the CLI (`npx paperclipai`) as the operator surface; define the integration seam (heartbeat + ticket + budget contracts).

items.title: gateway: hermes and ollama team pins are unreachable — no routed task requires their capability
items.body:
Parent: #338

## Finding (from the four-provider gateway review, PR #335)

The `purebliss-team` routing group pins the `hermes` and `ollama` agents to
their providers, but **no `routing.yaml` route references a capability either
persona holds**, so those two pins are unreachable end-to-end.

Repro (offline, `build_team_gateway`):

```python
from e2e.wiring import build_team_gateway
from proxy.model import TaskRequest
w = build_team_gateway()
for agent, task in [("hermes","summarize"), ("hermes","code-review-verdict"),
                    ("ollama","summarize"), ("ollama","classify-route")]:
    r = w.gateway.dispatch(agent, TaskRequest(tenant_id="acme", task_type=task,
                                              input={"thread":"x","diff":"d","context":"c","input":"x"}))
    print(agent, task, "->", r.outcome)   # denied / denied / denied / denied
```

Every dispatch is `denied` at the capability boundary (the provider is never
called), because:

- routed task types: `classify-route` -> `orchestrate`,
  `code-review-verdict` -> `code-review`, `summarize` -> `research`;
- `hermes` capabilitySet: code-author / test-author / test-run / memory-ops;
- `ollama` capabilitySet: code-author / test-run / memory-ops.

`deepseek` and `paperclip` (both hold `research`) route fine; `claude` holds
orchestrate/code-review/research. Only hermes and ollama are unreachable.

## Suggested fix (needs lanes outside gateway/**)

Add a routed task type whose capability hermes/ollama hold (e.g. `test-run` or
`code-author`), which requires a published prompt module in `registry/prompts/**`
+ a `routing.yaml` route + the FinOps task class — `registry/**` is outside the
gateway/e2e lanes, so this is filed rather than fixed in PR #335.

Refs: `gateway/proxy/config/routing.yaml` (routingGroups.purebliss-team),
`registry/personas/cards/{hermes,ollama}.yaml`.

items.title: gateway: registry fallback shadows the proxy routing chain (four-provider path)
items.body:
## What

Review and e2e-test the four-provider gateway path (paperclip / hermes / deepseek / ollama) end-to-end, fix what is broken, and prove the funnel offline.

## Scope

- `gateway/providers/**` (paperclip.py, hermes.py, deepseek.py, ollama.py, base.py, config.py, registry.py, contract.py)
- `gateway/proxy/**` (wiring, routing.yaml, router/dispatch)
- `gateway/finops/**` (tiers.yaml, complexity)
- `e2e/**` (golden_path, negative_controls, _team_providers, wiring)

## Known defect to fix

`ProviderRegistry.chat` walks the per-provider `fallback` chain (default `("ollama",)` for every cloud provider) BEFORE the proxy's `routing.yaml` chain is exhausted. Result: `LOW: deepseek -> openai -> ollama` behaves as `deepseek -> ollama` at runtime, skipping `openai`/`anthropic`. The proxy dispatch loop owns the chain; the backend must execute ONE candidate without the provider's own fallback.

## Verify

- `make verify` (gate of record)
- per-suite pytest for `gateway/providers`, `gateway/proxy`, `gateway/finops`, `e2e`
- `python3 -m pytest gateway e2e -q` (combined; collection collision documented)

items.title: [fleet-task] Web single-pane-of-glass: access control + tenant scoping for the live dashboard
items.body:
**GOAL:** Gate the web single-pane-of-glass behind tenant identity and RBAC so one tenant can never see another tenant's org, lanes, or claims. Success = an unauthenticated request is refused, a tenant scopes to its own rows, and only an admin sees the cross-org roll-up.

**Context:** The terminal dashboard has no access control because it is a local tmux pane; a browser surface changes that threat model. `identity/rbac/` and `identity/cpapi/` already declare the roles and policies the platform will enforce; the SPoG must consume them rather than invent a second policy.

**Cannibalize vs build:**
- CANNIBALIZE: `identity/rbac/` (roles, policies), `identity/cpapi/` (control-plane API auth), `identity/entitlements/` (what a principal may see).
- BUILD: the SPoG-specific policy bindings (which projection rows a role may read), the middleware that scopes `/api/fleet/*` by the caller's tenant, and the admin roll-up path.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] an unauthenticated `GET /api/fleet/snapshot` returns 401 (checked by an integration test)
- [ ] a tenant principal receives only its own org's rows (checked by two tenants + a cross-read assertion)
- [ ] the admin roll-up endpoint is refused for a non-admin principal (checked by a role-matrix test)
- [ ] no secret or token is ever logged or rendered (checked by the secrets gate + a negative control)

Role: subagent
Epic: #160
Pillar: identity-rbac
Lane: identity-rbac
Model tier (FinOps): pro
Thinking effort: medium

items.title: [fleet-task] Web single-pane-of-glass: browser dashboard with filters, timelines, and the org roll-up (#151)
items.body:
**GOAL:** Ship the browser half of the web single-pane-of-glass: a dashboard page that renders the live projection with the same health coloring and sections as the TUI, plus the three things a terminal cannot do — filters, a historical timeline, and the multi-tenant org roll-up. Success = a browser renders live frames, filters by tenant/lane/rung, scrolls the event history, and shows the org roll-up from #151.

**Context:** The TUI is one pane, un-shareable, unfilterable, and has no history. The repo already has `portal/static/` (a served frontend) and the leaderboard's dashboard patterns to cannibalize; the OSS terminal dashboards (Textual/rich) document layout/refresh idioms to port, not to wrap.

**Cannibalize vs build:**
- CANNIBALIZE: `portal/static/` (app shell, asset pipeline), leaderboard dashboard patterns (live table, status badges, color semantics), Textual/rich layout idioms (widget composition, bounded refresh) — as patterns, not dependencies.
- BUILD: the fleet frame component (health-colored rungs, status summary, waves, events), the filter bar (tenant/lane/rung/severity), the timeline (from `/api/fleet/events`), and the org roll-up view (#151 aggregates).

**Acceptance criteria:**

items.body:
# Board-drain wave plan (regenerating)

> committed dispatch snapshot `.board/snapshot.json`.

---

## 0. Measured board state (evidence)

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Open issues (live board) | **46** |

therefore requires two mechanisms in combination:
1. **Frontier claims** — the one eligible issue in the active milestone, in number order (145 → 146 → 147 → 149 → 150 → 151).
2. **Brain directives** (`claim --directive <id>`, recorded in `.fleet/sent`) — for every off-frontier lane

---

items.title: make verify (gate of record) runs no pytest: a red declared suite can sit on master undetected
items.body:
## Summary

`make verify` is the **gate of record** (`AGENTS.md`, GR-12), but it runs 25 checks
and **not one of them is a pytest suite**. The declared test corpus
(`scripts/pytest-suites.txt`, 51 suites) is exercised only by `make gate` /
`make tests`. So a red suite can sit on `master` undetected by the gate every PR is
measured against — and two did:

* `fleet/tests/test_controls.py::test_decompose_files_children_and_dispatches_only_wave_1`
  was red on `master` at `9312c15` (it read the live GitHub board).
* `governance/lessons` is still red (tracked separately as #312).

`docs/QA-GATE.md` documents the split on purpose ("`make verify` — the repo's
8-check composite gate of record"), and `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` names the
same separation. The consequence is the opposite of the intent: the cheaper gate
that every PR is judged by cannot see a failing test at all.

## Evidence (clean `origin/master`, sha `9312c15`)

```
$ bash scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh
run-pytest-suites: 49 passed, 2 failed, 0 no-verdict (51 declared suite(s), sha 9312c15c43d3)
  FAIL  fleet  (pytest exit 1: FAILED fleet/tests/test_controls.py::test_decompose... 1 failed, 357 passed)
  FAIL  governance/lessons  (pytest exit 1: ...test_the_repositorys_own_ledger_is_green 1 failed, 128 passed)

$ make verify
verify: PASS (25 of 25 checks)
```

The second command is the finding: **the gate of record was green while two
declared suites were red.**

## Why it happened

`scripts/verify.sh` builds its `checks` array from shell/python gate scripts;
`scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh` appears only in `scripts/gate.sh`'s signal list.
Nothing in `make verify` invokes pytest, so "the gate is green" is a claim about
linters and docs, never about the tests.

## Fix

Wire the declared suites into `make verify`'s check set as a check that can
genuinely fail (a check with no failing path is a formality — no-false-green
doctrine). Vacuity must be proved by breaking a test and showing the gate go red
(`verify: FAIL (1 of N checks failed)`), not asserted.

## Residual / follow-up

1. **Only the `fleet` suite is wired now.** The remaining declared suites stay on
   `make gate` until `governance/lessons` is green — it fails its own ledger check
   for an unrelated board-hygiene defect (#312) and would false-red the gate of
   record for every unrelated lane. Once #312 closes, the rest should be wired too
   (ideally by `make verify` invoking `scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh` for the whole
   manifest, so there is one runner and no drift).
2. **A green run on a networked machine does not prove a test is hermetic.** The
   `fleet` failure above was only visible because the live board changed under it;
   a live call that happens to pass is invisible to every gate. Tests in the
   declared corpus must not reach the network or the live board — see the
   companion fix for the instance (#326) — and this should eventually be
   enforced mechanically rather than by review.

`fleet/tests/test_controls.py::test_decompose_files_children_and_dispatches_only_wave_1`
calls the **real** dependency gate. It stubs `gh_issue_create` and `dispatch`, but not:

* `brain.issue_is_closed()` — `fleet/brain.py:556`, which runs
  `gh api repos/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/issues/N --jq .state` (a live network call), reached
  through `handle_decompose` → `dispatch_ready_children`; and
* the board-snapshot refresh in `handle_decompose` — `fleet/brain.py:541`, which shells out to
  `governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github`.

The test hardcodes its children as issues 301/302/303, and **#301/#302/#303 are real,
now-CLOSED board issues** — so the gate reads the dependencies as satisfied and dispatches all
three instead of only the dependency-free wave.

A unit test must not touch the network or depend on the live board: it is flaky, it is silently
coupled to board state that changes without the code, and here it made the `fleet` suite **red on
`master`**.

## Reproduction (clean worktree at `9312c15`; red back through `94b6cf1`, `0ff8adf`, `ebcf0df`)

```
$ python3 -m pytest fleet/tests/test_controls.py::test_decompose_files_children_and_dispatches_only_wave_1 -q
>       assert dispatched == [301], "only the dependency-free wave is dispatched now; b and c wait"
E       AssertionError: only the dependency-free wave is dispatched now; b and c wait
E       assert [301, 302, 303] == [301]
1 failed in 1.96s
```

Live board at the moment of reproduction: `301: closed`, `302: closed`, `303: closed`.

It is non-hermetic in a second, louder way: running the suite **rewrites the tracked
`.board/snapshot.json`** (729 insertions, a new `generated_at`) as a side effect of the
`--from-github` refresh — a unit test mutating a committed board artifact.

Measured with the whole fleet suite under a neutered `gh` (shim on `PATH` that exits 127):

```
BEFORE (9312c15) : 1 failed in 0.34s      # the test cannot pass without the network
AFTER  (fixed)   : 358 passed in 4.29s    # whole suite, no gh, no sockets
```

## Audit of the rest of `fleet/tests/**`

Instrumenting `subprocess.run`/`Popen` argv and `socket.connect`/`create_connection` across the
whole suite attributes every touch to the test that made it. Exactly **one** test reaches the
network — this one. The other subprocess calls are local stub runners
(`refusing-channel.py`, `probe-channel.py`, `stub-channel.py`, `git -C <tree> rev-parse`), and
there are **zero** non-loopback socket connects.

## Fix

Stub both live seams in the test: `brain.issue_is_closed` (returning "nothing is closed yet", so
the stub states the intent) and `brain.subprocess.run` (the snapshot refresh). Assert the
dependency gate was consulted, so the test cannot pass vacuously.

## Verify

```
set -o pipefail; python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "PYTEST RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

**GOAL.** One read-only projection answers "what is in flight, what is orphaned, what is shelved, what is wedged" across the fleet's stores — for a human operator and for an agent deciding what to do next.

**The gap, measured.** The fleet now keeps its state in five places, each added by a different lane: lane identities in `.fleet/lanes/`, session heartbeats in `.fleet/sessions/`, closure journals in `.fleet/lifecycle/`, claims in `.board/claims.jsonl`, and authorisation directives in `.fleet/{sent,done}/`. `fleet/console.py` is a dashboard for the **rungs only** (rung logs, monitor heartbeat, wave files) and joins none of them. Answering a single question this session — "is anything of mine still holding a lane?" — meant shelling into three CLIs, reading a ledger, and listing worktrees by hand; an agent with no operator does not do that, which is how an orphaned `ao-263-*` lane survived hours.

items.body:
**GOAL.** One declared policy for every timeout and lease in the fleet, with the relationships between the numbers stated.

**The gap, measured.** The fleet now runs at least four unrelated timings that must be *consistent with each other* and are declared in four different modules: the rung heartbeat is stale after **120s** (`fleet/channel.STALE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS`), a session heartbeat is an orphan after **15 minutes** (`governance/reconcile.DEFAULT_TTL_MINUTES`), a claim is reapable after **45 minutes** (`governance/dispatch` reap default), and a claim's own lease is **24 hours** (`--ttl-hours`). Their relationships are load-bearing and unstated: the session TTL must exceed the rung heartbeat (or a live lane is judged dead between beats), and the claim TTL must exceed the session TTL (or a claim is reaped while its lane is still legitimately running). This session both tuned and depended on those numbers and had to derive the relationships by reading three modules.

items.body:
**GOAL.** A finding the reconciliation worker or the lifecycle audit produces reaches the board, instead of living only in a cron log.

**The gap, measured.** `governance/reconcile` deliberately **shelves** a lane whose work exists nowhere else — keeping its worktree, its branch and its claim — precisely because it refuses to trade unmerged work for an unlocked issue. That choice is correct and the lane is reported **on every pass**; but "reported" means a line in `.fleet/reconcile.log` that nobody reads. The same is true of `governance/lifecycle`'s audit, which this session ran by hand and found 129 findings across the board, including a lane (#263) whose worktree had been orphaned by a killed run hours earlier. A control that reports into a log is a control that a fleet with no human in the loop never sees.

items.title: [fleet-task] Capability drift: a running rung must report capabilities it does not implement
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
**GOAL.** The fleet reports when a running rung does not implement capabilities the repository declares — not only when its commit drifts.

**The gap, measured.** After isolation (#263), lifecycle (#269) and reconciliation (#304) merged, the running sister loop kept executing pre-merge code: `governance/reconcile/cli.py status` reported `0 session(s)` in the live checkout because the loop had never stamped a session heartbeat, and the only signal was `watchdog decide() == "drifted"` — which compares *commits*, is reported per rung, and says nothing about **which capabilities are missing**. An operator cannot tell "the loop is old" from "the loop is old and therefore lanes are not being beat, so orphans will never be flagged". A capability that ships but is not live is a silently absent control.

- [ ] The signal distinguishes three cases: rung down, rung on drifted code, rung on current code **missing a declared capability** — each with its own remediation.
- [ ] `scripts/check-fleet-runbook.sh` (or the runbook gate) documents the restart step and the check provokes a missing capability and requires it to be reported.

items.title: ADR-0012 amendment: record the Hermes runtime fork explicitly (map the policy, do not couple the runtime)
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
**GOAL — record, in ADR-0012, that the chosen path is "map the policy, do not couple the runtime", and back it with the measured runtime facts about `hermes-agents`.** One file changes: `docs/decision-records/ADR-0012-hermes-paperclip-boundary.md`. The decision already exists (merged in #303); it is **implied rather than explicit** about the runtime fork, and a reader cannot tell from the record whether the fleet is meant to *depend on* the Hermes service at run time. This issue makes that explicit, so a later reader does not have to re-derive it.

**Constraints / non-negotiables.** Edit **one** file (`docs/decision-records/ADR-0012-hermes-paperclip-boundary.md`); the ADR index row in `docs/decision-records/README.md` may be added if that file is free. `vendor/` is a pinned read-only submodule — cite it in backticks, never as a markdown link (it is not populated in a fresh worktree, so a link fails `docs-lint`). Keep the existing Status / Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives / Migration structure; do not rewrite unrelated content. `make verify` is the gate of record (GR-12).

**Context — the fact behind the decision was never stated.** ADR-0012 declares the vendored `hermes-agents` module the owner of the orchestration *contract*, and forbids editing `vendor/`. What it never says is whether `hermes-agents` is something the fleet **runs against**. An open question kept being re-asked, so the fact was measured (Part A below) and is recorded here as the supporting evidence.

## Part A verdict — measured 2026-09-13

**`deployable-but-not-running`.** It is genuinely deployable as a service; it is not evidenced as running, and it is **not wired into this repo at all**.

Measured evidence:

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| It is a real service | `kushin77/hermes-agents` has `Dockerfile` (multi-stage), `docker-compose.yml` (service `hermes-agent`, `ports: "${PORT:-9501}:9501"`, healthcheck `GET /health`), `src/hermes_agent/app.py` (Flask), `src/hermes_agent/config.py` (`PORT` default **9501**), and `terraform/cluster/` + `scripts/deploy-to-production.sh`. |
| It is not evidenced as running | Zero releases and zero tags; the only protected environment is **`staging`** (no `production` environment exists); every recorded deployment is dated **2026-05-01** and every `deploy.yml` run concluded **failure** (10/10, newest 2026-07-19); the repo's own CI is failing as of 2026-09-13. |
| This repo does not deploy it | `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/hermes-agents/module.json` declares `"distribution": { "terraform": null }`; `hermes` appears **nowhere** under `infra/**`; there is no compose file or Dockerfile in this repo for it. |
| The gateway is **not** wired to it | `gateway/providers/config.py` maps `hermes` -> `http://localhost:8080/api/chat` with model `hermes3` (inheriting `OllamaProvider`, `gateway/providers/hermes.py`). The hermes-agents service speaks Flask on **9501** with `/health`, `/api/capabilities`, `/api/router`, `/api/tiering`. The string `9501` occurs **nowhere** in this repo. The gateway's `hermes` provider is an Ollama-protocol endpoint serving the Hermes-3 *LLM* — a **namesake**, not the routing service. |

Residual uncertainty: a live `/health` probe of the private cluster (VIP `192.168.168.50`, nodes `.31`/`.42`) is not reachable from this sandbox, so *currently running* rests on deployment history rather than a direct probe. That is named, not hidden.

## Part B — the decision test being recorded

1. **Is it deployable / running?** — Part A: deployable, not evidenced running, not wired here.
2. **Do we accept the fleet's control loop depending on it at runtime** (latency, failure, tenancy)? — No.
3. **Is Hermes a product to dogfood, or an internal pattern library?** — A pattern library.

Path: **map the policy, do not couple the runtime.** Counterfactual: if Hermes is a product to dogfood, that is a *different* ADR — "Hermes is the runtime routing authority; the fleet is a client" — a **migration**, not a mapping. Failure mode: **half-coupling** (two authoritative routing engines) is the worst outcome. Seam that keeps the swap cheap: the `RoutingPolicy` port (#300/#301).

## Deliverable

- [ ] ADR-0012 amended with: the three-fact decision test, the explicit counterfactual, the half-coupling failure mode, the `RoutingPolicy` seam, and the Part A verdict as supporting evidence. (checked: `git diff --stat` on the PR shows exactly one file, or two with the index row)
- [ ] `make verify` green on the merge commit. (checked: quoted gate output)

items.title: EPIC: ai.purebliss.app is its own webui — the OS is an addon (like other tenants), not the destination
items.milestone: Shared-Frontend Portal + UI
items.body:
## Objective (operator directive)
`ai.purebliss.app` must be **its own webui version**. The OS (`os.purebliss.app`) is
only an **addon/overlay inside it**, like the other tenants' frontends — not the
destination. Today, logging in at `ai.purebliss.app` lands the user in the master OS
(brand "OS Portal", origin `os.purebliss.app`) — i.e. not ai's own webui.

## Measured root cause (2026-09-13)
- `shared-frontend` `registry/modules.json` declares **ONE** portal for every origin:
  `portal: { name: "OS Portal", origin: "https://os.purebliss.app" }`; every container
  (os, gws, ai) reads that same registry. The shell only *displays* `portal.origin`
  (`shell/src/App.tsx:570`) — there is no code that navigates to `os.purebliss.app`,
  and the auth-hub relay honours the state's `return_url`/`backend_callback_url`
  (`auth-hub` `files/server.js:297`), so the "forward" is the **identity**, not a hop:
  ai renders the master OS's webui.
- Per-origin customization today is only **module scoping** (`OS_PRIMARY_MODULE` +
  `AUTH_CLIENTS_JSON`), the documented "dedicated origin" pattern used by
  `gws.purebliss.app` (`docs/RUNBOOK_GWS_PUREBLISS_ENABLEMENT.md`). There is no
  per-origin **portal identity** (name/origin/primary) and no way to present the OS
  itself as an addon.

## Desired model
- `ai.purebliss.app` = the agent-ecosystem portal: its own name/origin/branding/primary
  surface (the five-agent `purebliss` team, EPIC #253), not the master OS identity.
- `os.purebliss.app` = reachable **as an addon** within that portal (mounted like the
  other tenant frontends: a tab/iframe module entry), not the shell that owns the page.
- A login at `ai.purebliss.app` stays on `ai.purebliss.app`.

## Children (one issue = one lane = one branch)
- [shared-frontend] per-origin portal identity + expose the OS as an addon module.
- [shared-services] declare the `os-ai` container's portal identity and verify live.

## Definition of done
A login at `ai.purebliss.app` renders ai's own portal identity, with the OS available as
an addon; no navigation to `os.purebliss.app` occurs on load; gates green in both repos;
verified live.

items.title: governance/lessons: 'incident-labelled issue #141 was closed with no RCA record' keeps make gate red on master
items.body:
## Summary

`make gate` (the stronger composite: verify + per-suite isolated tests + drift + negative controls) is currently **RED on `master`**, in a suite unrelated to any single lane, and nothing reports it: `make verify` — the gate of record in `AGENTS.md` — does not run the pytest suites, so the suite that fails is only exercised by `make gate` / `make tests`.

`governance/lessons` fails its own ledger check: an incident-labelled issue was closed with no RCA record.

## Reproduction (on a clean checkout, as #288's evidence standard requires)

Reproduced identically on three trees — the pre-change base `a64f144` (which contains none of the #284 files), the #284 lane commit, and merged master `a7e7312`:

```
$ git worktree add --detach /tmp/ao284mech/lessons-proof a64f144
$ cd /tmp/ao284mech/lessons-proof
$ ls fleet/tests/test_isolation_guard.py scripts/check-pr-contract.sh
ls: cannot access '.../test_isolation_guard.py': No such file or directory
ls: cannot access '.../check-pr-contract.sh': No such file or directory

$ python3 -m pytest -q governance/lessons/tests/test_checker.py::test_the_repositorys_own_ledger_is_green
>       assert errors(report.findings) == []
E       AssertionError: assert [Finding(code...bel', line=0)] == []
E         Left contains one more item: Finding(code='board-incident-without-rca',
E           message='incident-labelled issue #141 was closed with no RCA record',
E           subject='#141', severity='error',
E           remediation='record the incident and its RCA, or remove the label', line=0)
governance/lessons/tests/test_checker.py:574: AssertionError
FAILED governance/lessons/tests/test_checker.py::test_the_repositorys_own_ledger_is_green
1 failed in 0.25s
```

Full declared-suite run on the merged content (`scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh`, `SUITE_TIMEOUT=120`):

```
run-pytest-suites: 49 passed, 1 failed, 0 no-verdict (50 declared suite(s), sha 046d33a2993f)
  FAIL  governance/lessons  (pytest exit 1: test_the_repositorys_own_ledger_is_green
        1 failed, 128 passed in 1.25s)
```

## The finding

```
board-incident-without-rca: incident-labelled issue #141 was closed with no RCA record
remediation: record the incident and its RCA, or remove the label
```

Either #141 needs its RCA recorded (or its incident label removed), or the ledger/quarantine needs to account for it. Because it is inside a gate, the whole `make gate` composite is red until it is resolved — including for lanes that touch nothing near `governance/lessons`.

Worth noting while fixing: the test pins `today=date(2026, 9, 15)`, i.e. a future date relative to this lane's clock (2026-09-13), so the verdict is a function of that fixed date plus the ledger — a change in either can flip it independently of any code change. Consider whether that date should be derived rather than hard-coded.

## Provenance

Found by the #284 lane while collecting post-merge evidence (PR #308). Not fixed there: `governance/**` is not that lane's to edit, and the reproduction above is what makes the attribution evidence rather than assertion.

items.title: Wire scripts/check-pr-contract.sh into the PR-time merge contract and a landed-history audit (#288 follow-up)
items.body:
## Summary

`scripts/check-pr-contract.sh` (added with #288) checks the three merge-contract
obligations that previously had no gate: the `Refs <owner>/<repo>#<n>` trailer on
every non-merge commit in a range, a filled-in `AI-assistance:` line in the PR
body, and a REPRODUCED pre-existing red (or an explicit `None`). It is **not
wired into `make verify`**, deliberately: in an ordinary working checkout there
is no PR body and the range `origin/master..HEAD` is empty, so wiring it would
turn every legitimate `make verify` red for a reason unrelated to the change
under test — the exact false-red the fleet doctrine forbids.

This issue is the follow-up that gives the gate an enforcement surface.

## What is needed

1. A PR-time hook (code-native — GR-15 forbids GitHub Actions) that runs:
   ```
   bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --body-file <the PR body> --range <base>..<head>
   ```
   The natural home is the merge contract already implemented in
   `governance/merge/` / `scripts/merge-gate.sh`, which is where a PR body is
   available and where the gate of record is already run.
2. A periodic audit of landed history, e.g. the ops runner invoking the same
   script over `<last-release-tag>..HEAD` with a body file that declares
   `None`, so drift is reported rather than silently accumulated.
3. Decide whether the lane audit (`governance/isolation/audit.py`, see the
   companion issue for #287) and this gate should share ONE trailer predicate
   instead of two implementations.

## The gate is not a formality while it waits

`bash scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --selftest` builds a scratch repository and
provokes every declared violation — subject-only reference, reference buried in
prose, missing trailer, unfilled `AI-assistance` placeholder, unreproduced
pre-existing red, missing body file, empty range — and requires each to be
refused by name. Verified output (9/9 OK, exit 0), and against the real commits
`8b97ab6` (accepted) / `6d89618` / `576edce` / `061690c` (refused, by name).

Provenance: the #284 lane, implementing #288.

items.title: fleet/terminal.py: loop() shadows the module-level verdict(), so a work directive crashes before its outcome record
items.body:
## Summary

`fleet/terminal.py`'s run path raises `UnboundLocalError` before it can emit a
run's OUTCOME record or report its result: `loop()` assigns a local named
`verdict` at line 936 (inside `if control:`), which shadows the module-level
`verdict()` function called at line 1192. For a work directive — the normal case
— line 936 never runs, so the name is unbound when the loop reaches the outcome.

## Evidence

Static proof (AST, on `origin/master` at `a64f144`):

```
$ python3 - <<'PY'
import ast, pathlib
tree = ast.parse(pathlib.Path("fleet/terminal.py").read_text())
fn = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "loop")
print("verdict bound (Store) at:", [n.lineno for n in ast.walk(fn)
      if isinstance(n, ast.Name) and isinstance(n.ctx, ast.Store) and n.id == "verdict"])
print("verdict called at:      ", [n.lineno for n in ast.walk(fn)
      if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Name) and n.func.id == "verdict"])
PY
verdict bound (Store) at: [936]
verdict called at:       [1192]
```

Runtime proof, from the behavioural #286 test (the loop is driven into one
dispatch with these seams stubbed — `singleton.guard`, `subprocess.run`,
`write_heartbeat`, `start_beating`, `claim_issue`, `provision_worktree`,
`run_once`, `release_in_flight`, `gate_evidence`, `landed_evidence`,
`closeout_issue`; NONE of them touches `verdict` or `control`):

```
E           UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'verdict' where it is not associated with a value
fleet/terminal.py:1192: UnboundLocalError
```

A directive that carries `control: "override"` does not fare better: it reaches
line 1192 with `verdict` bound to the STRING `"dispatch-override"`, so the call
becomes `TypeError: 'str' object is not callable`. In other words **every**
directive that reaches the outcome record crashes there, which is why the loop's
run path can currently never report a result.

## Consequence

- The `started` telemetry record (#233) is written at line 1136 and does escape;
  the outcome record at line 1194 is unreachable. `test_terminal_telemetry.py`
  could not have caught this — it greps the source text (`#286`).
- #286's suggested "assert a started AND a terminal record" cannot be satisfied
  until this is fixed; the #284 lane pinned the `started` emission only, and said
  so in the test docstring rather than weakening the assertion silently.

## Suggested fix

Rename the local (e.g. `control_verdict`) so the module-level `verdict()` is not
shadowed — a one-line change — and add a test that drives a work directive
through the run path to the outcome record.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed

`fleet/terminal.py` is not owned by the #284 lane (its brief lists the files it
owns, and this file is a hot lane shared with the prune/telemetry work), so per
the fleet doctrine the finding is attributed here rather than edited across a
lane boundary.

Provenance: found by the behavioural replacement test for #286 in the #284 lane.

items.title: governance/isolation: the ticket-trailer rule is a substring test, and landed lanes are never audited (#287 follow-up)
items.body:
Parent: #160

## Summary

`governance/isolation/audit.py` documents the history rule as *"every commit the
session authors carries `Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<n>`"*, and the README
says a commit that omits it is a named failure. The implementation is a substring
test over the whole commit message, so any mention anywhere — the **subject
line**, or prose — satisfies it, and a commit with no trailer paragraph at all
audits clean. Measured in #287 on `6d89618` and `576edce`: both carry the
reference only in the subject and the audit would accept them.

Second gap (unchanged): `scripts/check-session-isolation.sh` provisions lanes in a
**scratch** repository, and `governance/isolation/cli.py audit --all` is not wired
against the real repository, so landed history is never re-checked.

## New evidence (from the #288 lane, `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh`)

A position-based predicate was implemented for the PR-contract gate and run
against the four real commits #287/#288 name — it separates them exactly as the
issue's table does:

| commit | range check | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `8b97ab6` (#267) | `commit-pr-contract.sh --range 8b97ab6^..8b97ab6` | exit 0 — the ref is in the **trailing trailer block** (`Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#263` is its own paragraph, followed by `Co-authored-by:`) |
| `6d89618` (#270) | `--range 6d89618^..6d89618` | exit 1 — `commit-ref-only-in-subject:6d896189a694` |
| `576edce` (#268) | `--range 576edce^..576edce` | exit 1 — `commit-ref-only-in-subject:576edceca23d` |
| `061690c` (#236) | `--range 061690c^..061690c` | exit 1 — `commit-missing-ticket-trailer:061690ca33dc` |

One finding worth recording, because it constrains the fix: **`git
interpret-trailers --parse` cannot be the sole rule**. Git only recognises the
COLON form (`Refs: owner/repo#n`), while this repo's convention — and its own
exemplary commit `8b97ab6` — writes the colon-less form
(`Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#263`), which `interpret-trailers` does not
parse at all (measured on git 2.53.0: only `Refs: …` is emitted). A strict
`interpret-trailers` rule would therefore refuse the repo's own standard.

The rule that works is positional: the reference must be a line in the message's
**trailing trailer block** — the last paragraph(s) whose every line is a
`Token: value` line, a continuation, or the reference line itself. That block is
what `8b97ab6` has and what `6d89618`/`576edce` lack.

## Suggested fix

- Adopt the trailing-block predicate in `governance/isolation/audit.py` (or share
  one implementation with `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh`).
- Add the regression test #287 names: a commit whose only mention is in the
  subject must fail with `commit-missing-ticket-trailer`.
- Wire a real-repo audit (`cli.py audit --all`) into a code-native periodic job
  (GR-15: no GitHub Actions), treating "no lanes recorded" as CANNOT-ASSESS.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed

`governance/**` is owned by another lane, and this lane's brief is explicit that
it must not edit it (the #288 lane's constraint). Filing keeps the finding
attributable instead of silently overlapping.

Provenance: measured while implementing the #288 gate in the #284 lane.

items.title: [fleet-task] Reconcile orphaned sessions: per-session heartbeat, TTL sweep, worktree/branch teardown, lock release
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
**GOAL.** A reconciliation worker that turns a dead session into a clean workspace: per-session heartbeats, a TTL sweep that marks a session orphaned, teardown of its worktree and branch **without ever destroying unmerged work**, and release of the issue lock so another agent can take it.

**The gap, measured.** The fleet has three cleanup tools and none of them is driven by session liveness. `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` reclaims worktrees but only when a human or agent invokes it; `dispatch reap` releases claims on a 45-minute TTL that does not know whether the process is alive; `isolation close` removes a lane but only on request. Heartbeats exist **only per rung** (`sister.heartbeat.json`, `brain.heartbeat.json`) — a *dispatched lane* has no heartbeat of its own, so nothing can tell an orphaned lane from a busy one, and the worktree, branch and claim of a dead agent sit until someone notices by hand. Observed live on this board: an orphaned `ao-263-*` lane left by a killed run, and a claim that had to be reaped manually.

**Mapping to this repo's mechanisms (no new infrastructure invented).** There is no MCP context store and no GPG lease here, so requirement 4 is met by their real analogues: the **claim ledger** (`governance/dispatch/`, `.board/claims.jsonl`) is the issue lock, and the **worktree-scoped session signature** (`governance/isolation/`) is the lease. Releasing the claim is what puts the issue back in the pool; discarding the lane record invalidates the session identity.

Role: subagent
Epic: #160
Pillar: autonomous-ops
Lane: governance-reconcile
Model tier (FinOps): pro
Thinking effort: medium
Verify: `make verify`

Chain markers:

    Parent: #160
    Part-of: #160
    Blocked-by: none

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Heartbeat.** A session stamps `.fleet/sessions/<session_id>.json` — session id, issue, agent, lane, worktree, branch, pid, timestamp — and refreshes it on an interval while it runs; the file's `at` advances and the record is cleared on clean exit (`pytest governance/reconcile/tests`). The fleet loop stamps one for every lane it dispatches.
- [ ] **TTL sweep.** A session is marked orphaned when its heartbeat is older than the TTL (default 15 minutes) **or** its pid is gone; a fresh heartbeat behind a missing pid is reported, never silently reclaimed. Killing a process makes the next sweep flag that session id.
- [ ] **Teardown, with the safety rule that unmerged work is shelved, never destroyed.** If the lane's HEAD is not preserved outside the worktree, the worker keeps the worktree, records the session as `shelved` and reports it. If it is preserved, the worker removes the worktree, deletes the branch (local and remote) and forgets the lane record.
- [ ] **Lock release.** The claim is released so another agent can claim the issue again, and the session record is cleared — verified by querying the claim ledger for a live claim after the sweep.
- [ ] **Worker.** `sweep --apply` performs the pass; `watch` runs it as a daemon on an interval; it is wired into the repo's cron (code-native — no GitHub Actions workflows, GR-15).
- [ ] `scripts/check-reconcile.sh` (in `make verify`) provokes every branch of the safety rule: a live session is untouched, a stale one is flagged, a dead-pid one is flagged, an unpreserved lane is **not** destroyed, a preserved one is reclaimed, and the claim is released. A rule that cannot fail is a formality.
- [ ] Declared institutionally in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/GOVERNANCE.md`; the gate fails if a declaration is removed.

Evidence
