items.title: EPIC: Fleet ↔ Hermes/Paperclip alignment roadmap
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
**GOAL — make the fleet's ownership boundary with the vendored `hermes-agents` and `paperclip` modules explicit, stated once, and enforced.** This EPIC is the parent of the roadmap that lands that boundary: it records **ADR-0012** (the decision), then carries the three child issues that implement it. Success is one declared owner for dispatch, capability-routed dispatch through the registry personas, and a reporting surface aligned to paperclip's planning/status-report pattern — reached as a **non-blocking adapter**, with the fleet running throughout.

**Constraints / non-negotiables.** `vendor/` is a pinned read-only submodule: it is never edited (GR-5). Harvested patterns are recorded with GR-10 provenance in [`docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md`](https://github.com/kushin77/agent-orchestrator/blob/master/docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md). One issue = one lane = one branch (GR-3); no two lanes share a file. Every child must pass its own `Verify:` command **and** `make verify` before it is claimed done (GR-12).

**Context — the boundary is real and was never written down.** The vendored module `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/hermes-agents` declares itself as *"Agent routing, capability registry, escalation, and model-tiering patterns for multi-tenant agent orchestration and persona-driven task execution"* (features: `capability-registry`, `task-routing`, `model-tiering`, `escalation`). `fleet/brain.py` hand-implements exactly that surface — `choose_model()` derives the FinOps block from `fleet/profiles/brain.profile.json`, `needs_high_floor()` escalates a security/secrets/auth/IaC lane, and `governance/dispatch/` performs the capability/dispatch bookkeeping. `vendor/CMR/catalog/modules/paperclip` declares *"Planning and reporting workflow patterns for roadmap tracking, project health, and status-report discipline across governed workstreams"*, which is what the console dashboard, the wave plans and the status lines already do. The gateway adapters `gateway/providers/hermes.py` and `gateway/providers/paperclip.py` are **inference-only** and carry no routing authority — they are not the subject of this decision. The gap this EPIC closes is that no decision record said any of this.

---

## Decision (ADR-0012 — reproduced here as the EPIC's governing decision)

**The orchestration layer has a declared owner: the vendored `hermes-agents` module.** The fleet adopts that module's routing / capability-registry / escalation / model-tiering contract as the vocabulary of record for dispatch, cannibalizes its patterns under **GR-10** provenance into `fleet/` and `governance/dispatch/`, and **never edits `vendor/`** — the submodule is a pinned read-only source (GR-5). `paperclip` owns the **reporting** half of the same boundary — planning, roadmap tracking and status-report discipline — not the routing half.

**(a) Ownership is declared, not implied.** `hermes-agents` is the declared owner of the orchestration layer. The fleet's `choose_model` / tier-floor / escalation / dispatch behaviour is a **consumption** of that contract, recorded with GR-10 provenance, never a competing implementation to be grown independently.

**(b) Work is routed by capability from the registry personas.** Dispatch selects the worker by the capability the work needs, read from the registry personas that are actually dispatched:

| Work | Persona | Tier | Lanes |
|---|---|---|---|
| code / test / PR authoring | `registry/personas/cards/hermes.yaml` (`code-author`, `test-author`, `test-run`) | **MED** | `hermes`, `code-authoring` |
| research / docs / reporting | `registry/personas/cards/paperclip.yaml` (`research`, `docs-authoring`) | **LOW** | `paperclip`, `knowledge` |

The personas are registered by `registry/profiles/seeds/hermes.1.0.0.yaml` / `paperclip.1.0.0.yaml` and bundled in `registry/packs/releases/purebliss-team.1.0.0.yaml`. Tier escalation stays a floor, never a ceiling: the high-floor rule (security / secrets / auth / production-IaC never starts below HIGH) survives this decision unchanged.

**(c) The reporting surface aligns with paperclip.** The console dashboard, wave plans and status reporting adopt paperclip's planning / roadmap-tracking / status-report discipline as their pattern source, so the reporting half of the fleet has one declared owner too.

**(d) Migration is a non-blocking adapter — the fleet keeps running.** No stop-and-swap, no big-bang rewrite, no freeze: the alignment lands as an adapter over the behaviour that is already live. A child issue that cannot be landed without stopping the fleet is out of scope for this EPIC.

**Out of scope (stated so it is not conflated):** `gateway/providers/hermes.py` and `gateway/providers/paperclip.py` are **inference-only** provider adapters (Ollama-compatible `/api/chat` and OpenAI-compatible `chat/completions` wire shapes). They carry no routing authority, and this decision does not change them. Provider selection (`agent → provider`, the `routingGroups.purebliss-team` map in `gateway/proxy/config/routing.yaml`) is a **different layer** from capability routing (`work → agent`, the brain's `choose_model`) — the two are deliberately kept separate.

## Children (this EPIC's roadmap)

Created by this decision, in dependency order — each carries its own `Verify:` and acceptance criteria:

- [x] #303 — **Land ADR-0012** (this record) as a merged, accepted decision record. Owns `docs/decision-records/ADR-0012-hermes-paperclip-boundary.md`. The ADR has its own issue so this EPIC stays open for its implementation children — the pattern ADR-0011 followed when #161, not the M26 EPIC #160, owned that record.
- [ ] #300 — **Dispatch by capability: the brain consults the registry personas** (hermes → code/test/PR @ MED; paperclip → research/docs/reporting @ LOW). Owns `fleet/brain.py`, `fleet/profiles/brain.profile.json`.

**Lane disjointness (GR-3) — why these can run in one wave.** The children touch **no shared file**: #303 holds the ADR, #300 holds the selection (`fleet/brain.py`, `fleet/profiles/brain.profile.json`), #301 holds the dispatch chain and is the **single writer** of `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` (it records both provenance sections, so the paperclip harvest is handed to it rather than racing it), and #302 holds the reporting surfaces. Where a file is already owned by open work outside this EPIC, the child declares the edge instead of racing it — #300 is `Blocked-by: #274`, which owns `fleet/brain.py` in the current wave.

These live elsewhere and are **referenced here, never re-filed**. State is as measured on 2026-09-13 (five are already closed — recorded so the EPIC does not overstate open work):

**Related, distinct, and explicitly not duplicated:** #145 (cannibalize agent-profile / SME / persona code into the **registry**) and #149 (port SME-squad routing + capability/route/tier FinOps configs into the **gateway**) own the registry and gateway surfaces; this EPIC owns the **fleet dispatch + reporting** surface. #253/#254/#255 built the five-agent team's gateway routing, registry artifacts and personas; this EPIC decides who **owns** that layer and how the fleet **consumes** it.

items.body:
**GOAL.** Close-out must report its final audit against the *fresh* state of the item, not the pre-close snapshot it started from.

**The gap, measured.** The close-out for #269 performed every action correctly — merged, journal evidence, deleted the source branch, released the claim, closed the issue, reclaimed the lane — and then reported `NOT-OK` with five findings, because the executor's final audit re-read the *stale* item it had collected before any of those effects ran. The tests missed it because the fixture operations port mutates the item in place, so the re-audit saw the truth; the real operations port acts on GitHub and the filesystem, so the re-audit saw the past. This is the inverse of the false green the module exists to prevent: a fully successful close that reads as a failure.

items.title: PR-body and commit-trailer obligations have no template and no gate
items.body:
## Summary

Two obligations of the merge contract have no scaffolding and no gate, so they are
advisory-only in practice and were missed on real merges:

1. `docs/GOVERNANCE.md` §AI-assistance declaration: *"every AI-originated PR carries
   an `AI-assistance: <runtime> (<mode>)` note"* and `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md` states
   the PR body includes `Closes #<n>` **and** an AI-assistance declaration.
2. `AGENTS.md` golden rule 1: commits carry `Refs <owner>/<repo>#<n>`.

There is no `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (only `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`,
`copilot-instructions.md`, `dependabot.yml`, `workflows/`), and `grep -rl
"AI-assistance" scripts/ governance/ Makefile` returns nothing — no check reads a
commit trailer or a PR body.

## Measured outcome on four recent fleet merges

| PR | issue | `Refs` trailer on the merge commit | `Closes #<n>` | `AI-assistance:` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #236 | #232 | missing | yes | **missing** (only a `🤖 Generated with Claude Code` footer) |
| #270 | #233 | subject-only | yes | **missing** (same footer) |
| #267 | #263 | yes | yes | yes (tier + directive named — exemplary) |
| #268 | #265 | subject-only | yes | yes (tier named) |

So 3 of 4 landed commits do not carry a trailer, and 2 of 4 PRs do not carry the
declared note. #267 is the standard to aim at.

The same review found the evidence discipline inside PR bodies varies more than the
gate requires: #267 and #268 both *reproduced* a red gate on a clean checkout of
the base commit before attributing it elsewhere (exactly right), while #236 merged
with `make verify` at `21/22` and **asserted** its single failure was a pre-existing
stale claim-ledger entry without quoting a reproduction command.

## Suggested fix

- Add `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` with the required body: `Closes #<n>`,
  `AI-assistance: <runtime> (<mode>)`, and a `Verify:` block for real command output.
- Add a machine check for it (code-native, per GR-15 — no Actions): a
  `scripts/check-commit-trailers.sh` over the commits in a PR's range asserting the
  `Refs` trailer, and/or an equivalent check in the merge gate. The
  `check-session-isolation.sh` gate is the model: it should be able to fail on a
  subject-only ref (see the companion issue on the audit's substring predicate).
- State the standard for a *pre-existing* red gate explicitly: it is proven by a
  quoted reproduction on a clean checkout of the base commit, not by assertion.
  #267/#268 are the precedent to cite.
- Also worth closing the loop on the issue side: #263 was closed with all six
  acceptance-criteria checkboxes still `- [ ]` and its `Evidence` section still
  reading `(paste the real make verify output here)`. The evidence lived only in the
  PR body. Closing an issue with evidence pasted into the issue (or an explicit
  pointer) makes the ticket self-contained.

## Provenance

Found while reviewing the evidence and process rigor of PRs #236, #270, #267, #268
at the request of the fleet review.

`Verify:` the new PR template is rendered on a fresh PR, and the new trailer check
fails on a commit whose only `Refs` mention is in the subject (e.g. `6d89618`) and
passes on one with a real trailer (e.g. `8b97ab6`).

items.title: lane audit accepts a ticket ref on the subject line, and real lanes are never audited
items.body:
Parent: #160

## Summary

`governance/isolation/audit.py` documents the history rule as *"Every commit the
session authors carries `Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<n>`"*, and the README
says a commit that omits it is a named failure. The implementation is a substring
test over the whole commit message:

```python
missing = [sha for sha, message in authored_commits(worktree, identity.author_email)
           if identity.trailer not in message]
```

Any mention anywhere in the message satisfies it — including the **subject line**,
and including prose. A commit with no trailer paragraph at all audits clean.

## Evidence

A lane provisioned with the real module, one commit whose subject carries the ref
and whose body is empty:

```
COMMIT MESSAGE: 'Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#263: fix the thing\n\n'
TRAILER PARAGRAPH PRESENT: False        # no trailer line, no trailing paragraph
AUDIT VIOLATIONS: []                    # the audit reports the lane as isolated
```

This is not hypothetical: the commit that landed this very work has that shape.
`git log -1 --format=%B 6d89618` gives a subject of
`Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#233: wire per-run telemetry into fleet/terminal.py (#270)`
and no `Refs` trailer in the body — the audit's rule as written would accept it
even if it were audited (it is not; see below).

## Second gap: nothing audits the real repository's lanes

`scripts/check-session-isolation.sh` provisions lanes in a **scratch** repository
(`/tmp/session-isolation.$$.$(date +%s)`) and provokes violations there. That is
excellent as a gate on the mechanism, but `governance/isolation/cli.py audit --all`
is not wired into `make verify`, cron, or any other check against the real repo, so
the lane records under `.fleet/lanes/` and the commits actually on `master` are
never re-checked. The institutional rule currently has no enforcement surface over
landed history.

Measured on the four merges under review:

| commit | PR | `Refs …#<n>` as a trailer? |
|---|---|---|
| `8b97ab6` | #267 | yes — real trailer in the body |
| `6d89618` | #270 | no — ref is in the subject only |
| `576edce` | #268 | no — ref is in the subject only |
| `061690c` | #236 | no — no `Refs` reference anywhere in the body |

## Suggested fix

- Parse trailers properly rather than substring-matching: require the ref in the
  trailing trailer block (`git interpret-trailers --parse`, or an explicit
  last-paragraph match), and fail a commit whose only mention is in the subject.
  A test should assert the subject-only case is refused — that is the regression
  that would have caught the three commits above.
- Wire a real-repo audit into the gate (or a periodic code-native job, since
  GitHub Actions is disabled by GR-15): `python3 governance/isolation/cli.py audit
  --all` against the working repository, treating "no lanes recorded" as
  CANNOT-ASSESS rather than OK, so the check cannot pass vacuously.
- Keep the scratch-repo gate — it proves the mechanism; the missing piece is
  coverage of real history.

## Provenance

Found reviewing the quality of #267's lane-isolation artifacts at the request of
the fleet review. `scripts/check-session-isolation.sh` itself is a strong gate
(real provisioning, every violation provoked by name, plus a vacuity control) — the
gap is the strength of the trailer predicate and the absence of real-repo coverage.

`Verify:` with the trailer predicate tightened, a commit carrying the ref only in
its subject fails `cli.py audit` with `commit-missing-ticket-trailer`, and the
existing tests plus the new subject-only test pass.

items.title: test_loop_wires_record_run_into_the_run_path is a source-text grep, not a behavioural test
items.body:
Parent: #160

## Summary

`fleet/tests/test_terminal_telemetry.py::test_loop_wires_record_run_into_the_run_path`
asserts that a *string* appears in `inspect.getsource(terminal.loop)`:

```python
source = inspect.getsource(terminal.loop)
assert 'record_run(directive_id, issue, agent_id, "started"' in source
assert "record_run(directive_id, issue, agent_id, run_status" in source
```

It is a grep over source text, not a behavioural test. It passes as long as the
characters are present — including when the call is commented out, moved inside a
dead branch, or made unreachable. Measured: commenting the call out while keeping
its text leaves the test green.

```
# mutation: '        record_run(directive_id, issue, agent_id, "started", run_started_at)'
#        -> '        # record_run(directive_id, issue, agent_id, "started", run_started_at)'
mutated : PASS (mutant SURVIVED)  1 passed in 0.25s
restored: PASS                    1 passed in 0.39s
```

So the claim "the run path must call `record_run` for both the start and the
outcome" is not actually pinned by any test — deleting the emission of the start
record would ship silently.

Note this is the only non-vacuous-looking test of the four in that file; the other
three are genuinely behavioural (they fail when `record_run`'s status forwarding
or its schema-rejection handling is broken).

## Suggested fix

- Assert by effect: drive the record calls where they happen. Either invoke
  `terminal.loop` against a stubbed runner and an isolated `.fleet/` (the autouse
  fixture already redirects `telemetry.RUNS_LOG`), then read the JSONL back and
  assert a `started` record and a terminal `done`/`failed` record exist with the
  right `run_id`;
- or extract the two emissions behind a small seam that is callable in isolation
  and assert on it.
- Keep a shape assertion if useful, but pair it with an effect assertion.

The same pattern — `inspect.getsource` / substring assertions standing in for
behaviour — is worth a sweep across the fleet suite; it is the cheapest way for a
test to look like coverage while providing none.

## Provenance

Found reviewing the quality of fleet-produced artifacts (#233) at the request of
the fleet review. Landed in `6d89618` (PR #270).

`Verify:` the replacement test fails when the `started` emission is commented out
(today's substring test passes).

items.title: fleet/terminal.py record_run does not survive a write failure, contrary to its own docstring
items.body:
## Summary

`fleet/terminal.py::record_run` documents that a failed telemetry write must not
kill the run loop, but it only catches `telemetry.TelemetryError`. Any real write
failure — an unwritable directory, a full disk, a bad permission — raises `OSError`
(or a subclass), which propagates out of `record_run` and out of `terminal.loop`.

The docstring states the opposite contract:

```python
"""Append one per-run telemetry record; a bad append must not kill the loop.

Telemetry is an observability signal, not the run itself — if the log write
fails (disk full, bad permissions), the run outcome still gets reported over
the channel; only the extra record is lost.
"""
try:
    telemetry.append_record(...)
except telemetry.TelemetryError as exc:
    print(...)
```

`telemetry.append_record` does `path.parent.mkdir(...)` then `path.open("a")` —
both raise `OSError`, never `TelemetryError`. The named failure modes ("disk full,
bad permissions") are precisely the ones that are *not* caught.

## Evidence (clean detached worktree at `origin/master` `6d89618`)

Pointing `telemetry.RUNS_LOG` at a destination that cannot be written:

```
$ cd /tmp/qareview-232to270 && python3 -c "..."   # telemetry.RUNS_LOG -> <afile>/runs.jsonl
RESULT: raised FileExistsError -> [Errno 17] File exists: '/tmp/qareview-p1/afile'
IS OSError: True
IS TelemetryError: False
```

A `PermissionError` (read-only dir / unwritable file) behaves the same way — any
`OSError` escapes.

## Test gap

`fleet/tests/test_terminal_telemetry.py` covers only the schema-rejection path:

- `test_record_run_swallows_a_bad_status_instead_of_crashing_the_loop` — a bad
  *status* string (a `TelemetryError`), not a bad *write*.
- No test exercises the "disk full / bad permissions" case the docstring names.

## Suggested fix

- Catch `OSError` alongside `TelemetryError` in `record_run`, keeping the same
  "the run outcome is still reported" behaviour.
- Add a test that points `telemetry.RUNS_LOG` at an unwritable destination (e.g. a
  path whose parent is a regular file, which is deterministic and needs no chmod)
  and asserts `record_run` returns normally and writes the diagnostic to stderr.
- Adjust the docstring only if the code is deliberately meant to fail hard —
  telemetry is on the loop's hot path, so failing hard needs a stated reason.

## Provenance

Found reviewing the quality of fleet-produced artifacts (#232 / #233 telemetry) at
the request of the fleet review. Landed in `6d89618` (PR #270, "wire per-run
telemetry into fleet/terminal.py").

`Verify:` the new test fails against today's code (the `FileExistsError`
propagates) and passes once `OSError` is caught.

items.title: fleet isolation guard is inert: the conftest guard tests are never collected and cannot pass
items.body:
## Summary

The fleet suite's runtime-isolation guard is inert. Both guard tests live in
`fleet/tests/conftest.py`, and pytest does not collect `conftest.py` as a test
module — so the guard that is supposed to prove "no test writes into the live
`.fleet/slog.jsonl`" **never executes** in the suite the repo actually runs
(`pytest fleet/tests`, declared as the `fleet` suite in `scripts/pytest-suites.txt`
and run by `scripts/run-pytest-suites.sh` / `make tests`).

It is worse than uncollected: when invoked explicitly it **always fails**, and the
one assertion that would detect a real leak inspects a path that is never the live
log. Three independent defects, all on `origin/master` (`6d89618`).

## Evidence (measured on a clean detached worktree at `origin/master`)

**1. Not collected — the guard never runs.**

```
$ python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q --collect-only
224 tests collected in 0.38s
     is `test_a_test_write_lands_in_tmp_and_never_in_the_live_log` collected? NO
     is `test_every_channel_runtime_path_is_redirected` collected? NO

$ python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q -k "lands_in_tmp or every_channel_runtime_path"
224 deselected in 0.39s        # rc=5 — no tests collected for that selection

$ python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q
224 passed in 4.89s            # the guard contributes nothing to this number
```

**2. It cannot pass even when run.**

`channel._slog` serialises with `json.dumps`' default `ensure_ascii=True`, so the
probe's U+2014 em dash is written as `\u2014` and the raw substring is absent:

```
json line     : {"body": "isolation probe \u2014 this must never reach the live slog"}
probe in line : False        # U+2014 vs the 6-char escape
```

```
$ python3 -m pytest fleet/tests/conftest.py::test_a_test_write_lands_in_tmp_and_never_in_the_live_log
E  AssertionError: the probe did not go where the fixture points
E  assert 'isolation probe — this must never reach the live slog' in '{"body": "isolation probe \\u2014 ..."}'
1 failed
```

**3. The live-log assertion reads the wrong directory.**

`live_fleet_dir()` returns `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / ".fleet"`, which
from `fleet/tests/conftest.py` is `<repo>/fleet/.fleet` — not `<repo>/.fleet`:

```
WORKTREE        = /tmp/qareview-232to270
channel.SLOG    = /tmp/qareview-232to270/.fleet/slog.jsonl      <- the real live log
live_fleet_dir  = /tmp/qareview-232to270/fleet/.fleet           <- what the guard reads
MATCHES REAL LIVE LOG: False
```

So `if live.exists()` is never true and the leak assertion is unreachable. This is
the "a check that cannot fail is a formality" case (GR-12) — and the docstring
claims the opposite ("the guard test proves the cover is real").

**4. `RUNTIME_PATHS["monitor"]` is dead.** The fixture does
`module = sys.modules.get(name); if module is None: continue`, and no fleet test
imports `monitor` (every other mention is a string or dict key). Measured during a
full-suite run: `ABSENT: ['monitor']`. The documented promise — "a new test cannot
forget to patch one" — does not hold for any module that is not already imported
at fixture time; a test doing `import monitor` inside its body gets an
un-redirected module.

## Why this matters

The install-by-side-effect claim in the docstring — that running the suite once
appended 32 fabricated entries (`merged #171`, `done`) to the real
`.fleet/slog.jsonl` — is exactly the class of failure this guard exists to prevent,
and the guard as written would not have caught it. The event log is what
`fleet/health.py` reads and the brain tails, so a silent fabrication there is a
false-success channel.

## Suggested fix

- Move both guards into a collected module, e.g. `fleet/tests/test_isolation_guard.py`.
- Assert on the parsed record (`json.loads(line)["body"]`), not on the raw line, so
  JSON escaping cannot make the assertion unsatisfiable.
- Fix `live_fleet_dir()` to the repository root (`.fleet/` beside `fleet/`, not
  inside it) and assert the probe is absent from the **real** path.
- Make the fixture refuse to skip a module: import every `RUNTIME_PATHS` key
  itself (or fail the run if a key is absent from `sys.modules`), so a module
  cannot silently fall out of the cover.
- Add a negative control that proves the guard can fail — remove the `"channel"`
  entry from `RUNTIME_PATHS` and require the guard to go red.

## Provenance

Observed while reviewing the quality of fleet-produced artifacts (#232/#233/#234
telemetry, #267 lane isolation) at the request of the fleet review. The guard was
introduced by `f2c2f81` ("fix(fleet): the test suite no longer writes into the live
fleet's audit log (#215)"), and `RUNTIME_PATHS` was extended by #236 and #268.

`python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q --collect-only | grep -c isolation_guard` is

`"channel"` entry is removed.

items.title: fleet/terminal.py: graceful stop logs a spurious release FAILED because the claim is released twice
items.body:
## Symptom

Every graceful stop of the sister loop logs a **false failure** — `[terminal] release of #N FAILED: ...` plus a spurious `warn` escalation — even though the claim was released correctly. The claim is released twice on the SIGTERM path, and the second release is refused.

## Evidence / repro

Frozen review tree: `git archive 6d89618` (master), `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py` proof P9.

Two independent owners release the same claim:

* `fleet/terminal.py::handle_stop` (SIGTERM/SIGINT) → `stop_and_release(...)`, which calls `release_issue(issue, agent_id)`.
* the run's `finally` in `loop()` → `release_issue(issue, agent_id)` again (using the locals captured before the `try`).

`release` is deliberately not idempotent:

```
PROVEN  P9 second release REFUSED -> terminal's finally logs a spurious FAILED
         ClaimRefused(not-claimed): #4242 has no live claim
```

(`claims.release` raises `ClaimRefused("not-claimed", ...)` → `cmd_release` returns `EXIT_NOT_OK` → `release_issue` returns `(False, ...)` → the `finally` prints `release of #N FAILED` and escalates.) So the operator's audit trail says a graceful stop failed to release the claim when it did not — evidence that misleads during exactly the incident it was written to make legible.

## Proposed fix

* Make the release single-owner: have `stop_and_release` clear `IN_FLIGHT["issue"]`/`IN_FLIGHT["agent_id"]` (or set a `released` flag) so the `finally` skips a claim already released.
* Optionally treat `not-claimed` as a benign no-op in `release_issue` (a release of something already released is not a failure), while still surfacing `not-owner`.

## Non-blocking

Small refactor inside the sister loop; no new state, no protocol change. Safe to land while the fleet runs (takes effect at the next sister restart — not proposed as an immediate restart).

---
Provenance: adversarial read-only review of `fleet/*.py` at `6d89618`; harness `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py`. No repo files were modified.

items.title: fleet/: .fleet/ grows unbounded — no rotation or pruning for mailboxes, slog.jsonl or rung logs
items.body:
## Symptom

`.fleet/` grows without bound: nothing rotates or prunes the mailboxes, the JSONL ledger or the rung logs. The brain reads only the newest `--limit` replies, so the rest is dead weight that still costs a `glob` + `read_text` per entry elsewhere.

## Evidence / repro

Measured on the live checkout (read-only):

```
$ du -sh .fleet
13M	.fleet
$ for d in outbox sent done inbox reported runs brain/sent brain/done brain/outbox; do \
    printf "%-14s %s\n" "$d" "$(ls .fleet/$d | wc -l)"; done
outbox         2788
sent           42
done           34
inbox          1
reported       0
runs           1
brain/sent     13
brain/done     13
brain/outbox   13
$ ls -laS .fleet/*.jsonl .fleet/*.log | head -3
-rw-r--r-- 786786 .fleet/slog.jsonl
```

`grep -rln "rotate|prune|truncate" fleet/*.py` finds only `singleton.py`'s `os.truncate` of the lock file and `console.py`'s docstring — no `.fleet` retention anywhere. The only prune tool is `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`, which handles lane worktrees, not `.fleet`. `channel.slog.jsonl` is append-only and unbounded; `watchdog.log`, `brain.log`, `open-eye.log`, `monitor.log`, `sister.log` are append-only with no rotation; `.fleet/runs.jsonl` (telemetry) is append-only.

## Proposed fix

* A code-native `fleet/prune.py` (or a `fleet/cron.py` subcommand) that ages out `.fleet/{outbox,sent,done,brain/{sent,done,outbox}}` entries and rotates `slog.jsonl` / `*.log` / `runs.jsonl` beyond a retention window, **dry-run by default** with an `--apply` (mirroring `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`, which the Makefile already drives).
* Wire it to the cron-owned automation (`fleet/cron.py install` already owns one line; add a second marked line) so retention needs no human.
* Do not delete un-consumed inbox entries or a live run marker — only answered/consumed artifacts.

## Non-blocking

New script + a cron line; purely additive and safe while the fleet runs. No restart required.

---

items.title: fleet/terminal.py: run success is decided by substring-matching the model's prose, not by verification evidence
items.body:
## Symptom

The sister loop decides a run succeeded by **substring-matching the model's own prose** (`fleet/terminal.py::looks_refused`) and by the runner's exit code — it never machine-checks the evidence the run was asked to produce (the issue's `Verify:` command or a green `make verify`). A run that does no work but prints confident prose is reported to the brain as a `result` (success); a genuinely successful run that merely mentions the word `REFUSED` is escalated as a failure. This is the "evidence that could be fabricated" failure mode, against GR-12 / no-false-green.

## Evidence / repro

Frozen review tree: `git archive 6d89618` (master), `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py` proofs P10a/P10b.

```python
def looks_refused(output: str) -> bool:
    upper = output.upper()
    return "REFUSED" in upper or "NO WORK DONE" in upper or "NO REAL ISSUE" in upper
```

```
PROVEN  P10a a run that prints no evidence of work still counts as SUCCESS
         looks_refused('All checks are green. Opened PR '...)=False -> loop reports `result` (success)
PROVEN  P10b a genuinely successful run is escalated as a FAILURE on the word 'refused'
         looks_refused('channel send: REFUSED (replay de'...)=True
```

The `rc == 0 and not refused` branch writes a `result` (success) and `record_run(..., "done", ...)` — a verdict derived from words, not from a command that can fail.

## Proposed fix

* After the runner returns, have the loop derive the verdict from a **machine signal** it runs itself in the lane worktree: the directive's `verify` (or `make verify`) plus the real `gh` PR/merge state, and record that exit code in the telemetry record and the channel report.
* Keep the prose check only as an *additional* hint (never the sole basis), and make the report body carry the command + its output, not just the runner's tail.
* Give the check its own negative control: a run that produces no verification evidence must land in the non-success bucket.

## Non-blocking

Additive (a post-run verification step plus a wider telemetry detail field). Safe to land while the fleet runs; it changes behaviour only for runs that start after the next sister restart — **needs a restart window** to become live, and is not proposed as an immediate restart.

---

items.title: fleet/channel.py: cmd_order's anti-replay check can never fire (identical operator order accepted twice)
items.body:
## Symptom

`channel.py order`'s anti-replay check can **never fire**: it scans the sister's mailboxes while the operator-order path writes to the brain's. An identical operator order (same `id`, same `nonce`) is accepted twice, so a duplicated order double-dispatches the same issue.

## Evidence / repro

Frozen review tree: `git archive 6d89618` (master), `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py` proofs P4a/P4b.

`replay_conflict()` scans `SENT`, `INBOX`, `DONE`; `cmd_order` writes to `BRAIN_SENT` / `BRAIN_INBOX` and nothing ever copies the order into the sister's mailboxes. The same check *does* work for `send`, so the asymmetry is invisible unless exercised:

```
PROVEN  P4a identical operator order is ACCEPTED twice (replay check is a no-op for `order`)
         rc1=0 rc2=0 (both accepted despite identical id+nonce)
PROVEN  P4b same check DOES fire for `send` (asymmetry confirmed)
         send rc1=0 rc2=1
```

This is also a no-false-green issue: `cmd_order` calls a guard whose failing path cannot be reached on that call path.

## Proposed fix

* Parameterise `replay_conflict(message, directories)` (or have `cmd_order` pass `(BRAIN_SENT, BRAIN_INBOX, BRAIN_DONE)` and `cmd_send` pass `(SENT, INBOX, DONE)`), keeping the shared body.
* Add a regression test: two `cmd_order` calls with the same `id`/`nonce` must yield `0` then `1`.

## Non-blocking

Pure function change plus a test, no live-state dependency. Safe to land while the fleet runs.

---
Provenance: adversarial read-only review of `fleet/*.py` at `6d89618`; harness `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py`. No repo files were modified.

items.title: fleet/health.py: never probes the brain — reports healthy while the middle rung is dead
items.body:
## Symptom

`fleet/health.py` probes **only the sister**. With the brain — the middle rung, and the only thing that turns an operator order into a directive — completely dead, `health.py check` still reports `healthy` (exit 0). The health surface therefore contradicts `channel.py status`, which does check both rungs.

Secondary: the "activity" signal is the mtime of `.fleet/slog.jsonl`, which is only written when a message moves — so a fleet that is idle (nothing ordered) for longer than the window reads `degraded` although it is perfectly healthy.

## Evidence / repro

Frozen review tree: `git archive 6d89618` (master), `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py` proof P5.

```
PROVEN  P5 health reports healthy with the brain down (no brain probe)
         pgrep patterns=['fleet/terminal.py'] level=0 reasons=['loop running, slog fresh, no wedged claims']
```

`health.py` has exactly one process probe — `loop_running()` with `pgrep -f fleet/terminal.py` — and `code_drift()` reads only `channel.read_heartbeat()` (the sister's beat). Compare `channel.report_rung`, which is applied to **both** `brain.py` and `terminal.py` and returns NOT-OK on drift.

## Proposed fix

* Add a brain probe mirroring `report_rung`: `pgrep -f fleet/brain.py` + `fleet/brain.heartbeat.json`, including the same code-drift comparison.
* A dead/missing brain should be at least `degraded` (and `failing` when the sister is down too), since no order can be dispatched without it.
* Prefer a liveness signal (heartbeat age) over `slog` mtime for "no observed activity", so an idle-but-healthy fleet is not reported as degraded.

## Non-blocking

Additive check in a read-only module; `health.py` is called by the brain's non-work order path (`_health`) and by `control health`. Safe to land while the fleet runs.

---
Provenance: adversarial read-only review of `fleet/*.py` at `6d89618`; harness `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py`. No repo files were modified.

items.title: fleet/watchdog.py: respawn is reported without verification and a spawn failure crashes the pass (RESPAWN FAILED unreachable)
items.body:
## Symptom

`fleet/watchdog.py` reports `respawned` **without ever verifying that the rung came up**, and a spawn failure raises out of the pass instead of being reported. The `RESPAWN FAILED` branch is unreachable for the two loop rungs, so the watchdog's exit code can read green while nothing is running.

## Evidence / repro

Frozen review tree: `git archive 6d89618` (master), `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py` proofs P1a/P1b.

* `respawn()` ends `spawn(...)` then `return True` — unconditionally. `rung_action` renders `'respawned' if ok else 'RESPAWN FAILED'`, so `skip=ok` is always True.
* `spawn()` has no `try` around `open_log()`/`subprocess.Popen`, so an OS error (disk full, EAGAIN) escapes and takes the whole cron pass down — it never becomes `RESPAWN FAILED`.
* `watchdog_once` only sets `failed=True` when a line contains `FAILED`; for the rungs that can never happen.

```
PROVEN  P1a watchdog says 'respawned' although spawn() started nothing
         line='sister: missing (no loop process) — respawned' spawn() invoked=1 (no process started)
PROVEN  P1b spawn failure crashes the watchdog pass (never 'RESPAWN FAILED')
         raised OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
```

(A rung can also be spawned and immediately die — e.g. the singleton refuses, or `brain.py` hits the P2 crash — and the pass still reports `respawned`.)

## Proposed fix

* Catch `OSError`/`subprocess.SubprocessError` around `spawn()` and return `False`.
* Make `respawn()` verify: after spawning, poll `loop_pid(pattern)` (and the rung's heartbeat) for a bounded window and return `False` if the rung did not come up.
* Then `RESPAWN FAILED` becomes reachable, `watchdog_once` exits 1, and `python3 fleet/cron.py status` shows a real failure instead of a fabricated success.

## Non-blocking

Watchdog-internal change; it runs from cron/`fleet/cron.py run`. Safe to land while the fleet runs — it takes effect on the next cron tick.

---
Provenance: adversarial read-only review of `fleet/*.py` at `6d89618`; harness `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py`. No repo files were modified.

items.title: fleet/brain.py: a decompose order without parent_issue raises KeyError and kills the brain loop
items.body:
## Symptom

A malformed `decompose` order raises an unhandled `KeyError` inside `fleet/brain.py` and **kills the brain loop** (the process exits; nothing restarts it until the next watchdog tick).

## Evidence / repro

Frozen review tree: `git archive 6d89618` (master), `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py` proof P2.

`fleet/brain.py::handle_decompose` reads the parent with no guard:

```python
spec = (order.get("task") or {}).get("decompose")
if not isinstance(spec, dict) or not spec.get("children"):
    return False, "decompose order carries no children — nothing to file"
parent = int(spec["parent_issue"])          # <- KeyError when absent
```

Calling it with a children-bearing spec that omits `parent_issue`:

```
PROVEN  P2 brain.handle_order raises KeyError -> loop dies (unhandled)
         KeyError('parent_issue')
```

`handle_order` catches nothing, and `loop()` does not wrap `handle_order(order)`, so the exception propagates out of `loop` and terminates the process. `handle_decompose` also calls `gh_issue_create`, which raises `RuntimeError` on any `gh` failure — the same escape.

## Proposed fix

* Validate the decompose spec up front (`parent_issue` a positive int, `children` a non-empty list of objects) and return `(False, "<reason>")` — a refusal reported to the operator, not a crash.
* Wrap the `handle_order(order)` call in `loop()` so any unexpected exception is caught, reported through `channel.brain_reply(order, "result", ...)`, and the order is consumed; the loop then keeps running (doctrine: a refusal is a refusal, never a silent death).

## Non-blocking

Pure function/loop change, no live-state dependency. Safe to land while the fleet runs; takes effect on the next brain restart.

---
Provenance: adversarial read-only review of `fleet/*.py` at `6d89618`; harness `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py`. No repo files were modified.

items.title: fleet/brain.py: no graceful stop or heartbeat during work — a stale beat kills the brain mid-order and can re-dispatch it
items.body:
## Symptom

`fleet/brain.py` has **no graceful-stop handler and no heartbeat while it is working**, so the middle rung can be killed mid-order — and a kill in the wrong instant re-dispatches the order, duplicating work.

## Evidence / repro

Frozen review tree: `git archive 6d89618` (master), `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py` proof P8.

1. `fleet/brain.py` writes a heartbeat in exactly two places — line 549 (`idle`, once per poll) and line 582 (`dispatching`, immediately *before* `handle_order`). Nothing refreshes the beat while `handle_order` runs.
2. `fleet/brain.py` contains **no `signal` handler** and **no beater** (unlike `fleet/terminal.py`, which owns `RunBeater`). `handle_decompose` performs N `gh issue create` calls plus a `snapshot --from-github` refresh — easily longer than `channel.STALE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` (120 s).
3. `fleet/watchdog.py::decide` classifies a beat older than 120 s as `stale`, and `rung_action` respawns `stale` rungs unconditionally (only a *drifted* **sister** is protected by `run_in_flight()`). A `stale` brain is therefore SIGTERMid with no handler → immediate death mid-order.
4. `fleet/brain.py::loop` runs `handle_order(order)` → `channel.brain_reply(...)` → `channel.consume_order(order_id)` as three separate steps. A kill between the dispatch inside `handle_order` and `consume_order` leaves the order pending, and the next brain start re-reads it:

```
PROVEN  P8 re-reading one order dispatches it twice
         dispatches for the same order=['4242', '4242']
```

`dispatch()` re-composes a directive with no `id`/`nonce`, so `channel.send` stamps a fresh uuid4 and its replay check cannot help.

## Proposed fix

* Give the brain the same liveness discipline as the sister: wrap `handle_order` in a heartbeat beater (extract `terminal.RunBeater` into a shared `fleet/liveness.py`, or import it), so a long decompose cannot look stale.
* Install a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler that lets the current order finish (or at minimum marks it), and make the dispatch→consume step atomic from the loop's point of view: record a sent-marker *before* sending and consult it on restart (or consume the order as part of the dispatch), so a restart can never re-dispatch a directive it already sent.

## Non-blocking

Additive (a new shared module + wiring in `brain.py`). The change is safe to land while the fleet runs; it takes effect at the next rung restart (watchdog/`control restart`), not on the running loop — no immediate restart is required or requested.

---
Provenance: adversarial read-only review of `fleet/*.py` at `6d89618`; harness `/tmp/aofleet-proof.py`. No repo files were modified.

items.title: Portal login must be shared-frontend proper: consume the OS auth-gate session, delete the private login form

Parent: #271

## Objective
The agent-orchestrator **portal** (the surface behind `ai.purebliss.app`) must stop
implementing its own login and instead sit behind the shared-frontend auth-gate
("one front door"), establishing its session by **verifying the RS256
`os-session-token`** the auth-gate mints — the module-side path of `shared-frontend`
`docs/AUTH.md` §"Verifying a session token server-side".

## Scope (lane: portal — `portal/**` only; consume `identity/sso` read-only)
1. `portal/static/views/login.html` — **remove the demo email/tenant credential form**
   (and its hardcoded demo identities). An unauthenticated visitor must be sent to the
   OS auth gate; the portal renders no credential form. Either delete the page
   (redirect straight to `/auth/login`) or reduce it to a pure "Redirecting to sign
   in…" page that immediately navigates to `/auth/login`.
2. `portal/server/app.py` — front-door gating: in `_index()`, an unauthenticated
   document request returns **302 to `/auth/login`** (the OS gate), never to a local
   login view. **Remove `POST /api/console/login`** (the `_login` credential path).
   `_require_session` must verify the `os-session-token` (not a locally minted login
   session) and fail closed (401) otherwise.
3. `portal/server/sso.py` — replace the `SsoService` *login/relay* wrapper with an
   **auth-gate session verifier**: consume `identity.sso.tokens.verify_console_session_token`
   against the auth-gate's published JWKS (offline: a configured JWKS payload mirroring
   `GET /auth/.well-known/jwks.json`), enforce `purpose: os-session-token`, map verified
   claims (email/name/role) -> console Principal, preserve the ROOT_ADMIN allowlist
   semantics. Fail closed on any error.
4. `portal/tests/` — assert the shared-frontend auth contract:
   - a real `os-session-token` verifies and establishes the console session;
   - a **forged** token, and a **wrong-purpose** token (a session-cookie JWT or an
     OAuth `state` JWT replayed as a module token) are refused 401;
   - `POST /api/console/login` no longer exists (404);
   - an unauthenticated document request returns 302 `/auth/login`;
   - existing SSO/RBAC negatives stay green.

## Acceptance criteria
- No private credential form / login route remains in the portal.
- The portal session is established **only** from a verified auth-gate `os-session-token`
  (purpose-checked, RS256, JWKS-verified, fail closed).
- `make verify` green; `pytest portal/tests` green (all pre-existing tests included).

## Verify
python3 -m pytest portal/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider
make verify

items.title: [fleet-task] End-to-end GitHub lifecycle: every work item closes hygienically, all artifacts terminal
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
**GOAL — the GitHub process closes end-to-end, hygienically, by construction.** Every work item that reaches a terminal state must leave *every* artifact it created in its terminal state, and the machine must be able to prove it. Isolation (#263) guarantees a lane *opens* correctly; this guarantees it *closes* correctly — and that nothing is silently left behind.

**The gap, measured.** Closing the isolation lane was manual and drifted, every time: `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` printed `fatal: 'master' is already used by worktree at ...` and the remote branch survived until deleted by hand; the fleet's own loop re-claimed the closed issue and left a live claim plus a lane worktree behind; the authorisation directive had to be consumed manually; and refreshing the board snapshot exposed five open milestoned issues with no `class:` label. None of that was caught by a gate. Each was a *step in a process that nobody owned*.

Role: subagent
Epic: #160
Pillar: autonomous-ops
Lane: governance-lifecycle
Model tier (FinOps): pro
Thinking effort: medium
Verify: `make verify`

Chain markers:

    Parent: #160
    Part-of: #160
    Blocked-by: none

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `governance/lifecycle/` models the work-item lifecycle end to end — `filed -> claimed -> laned -> opened -> verified -> merged -> closed -> reclaimed` — and states the **closure invariants**: PR merged at a verified commit; source branch gone (local and remote); claim released; authorisation directive consumed; issue closed with real evidence; lane worktree reclaimed; declaring labels present. Each invariant is a named check, not prose.
- [ ] `closeout` executes the full close in dependency order and **verifies each artifact reached its terminal state** — it reports success only when every invariant holds, and it is idempotent and resumable, so a re-run after a partial close finishes the remaining steps instead of failing or double-acting.
- [ ] `audit` reports every non-hygienic item as a finding naming the item, the broken invariant and the remediation; it runs **offline** (no network, no containers) so it can live in `make verify`.
- [ ] `scripts/check-github-lifecycle.sh` (in `make verify`) proves each invariant can fail — one provoked violation per invariant, each detected by name — and that a hygienic item passes. It asserts the mechanism against repo fixtures, and ships **no committed point-in-time GitHub record**, so it cannot go green by being stale (the failure mode measured in `.board/snapshot.json`, tracked by #170).
- [ ] `fleet/terminal.py` drives close-out through the module, so a dispatched subagent cannot finish a run leaving a merged PR unmerged, an issue open, a branch undeleted, a worktree behind, or a claim wedged.
- [ ] The contract is declared institutionally in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/GOVERNANCE.md` and `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md`, and the gate fails if any declaration is removed.
- [ ] Legacy drift is **quarantined, not hidden**: items already tracked by an open governance issue (#170 snapshot staleness, #174 unlabelled issues) are grandfathered by name with their tracking issue, and any *new* item failing the same invariant fails the gate. The quarantine shrinks as legacy closes; it cannot grow silently.

items.title: Fleet live console: capture rung output, meaningful brain context, dashboard, and log into the live session
items.body:
## Problem

The operator has **no way to log into the live fleet session and see meaningful context**.

Measured:

- There is no tmux server running (`tmux ls` → none) and no rung runs in a tmux window, so
  there is nothing to attach to.
- `fleet/watchdog.py` respawns each rung with
  `subprocess.Popen(["setsid", "bash", script], stdout=DEVNULL, stderr=DEVNULL)` — every
  rung's output is **thrown away**. Nothing about the brain is observable anywhere.
- `fleet/brain.py` prints nothing useful on startup, nothing identifying the order it is
  handling, and nothing while idle — so even with a captured log the brain window would be
  a blank screen.
- `fleet/run-fleet.sh` starts a tmux session only when **both** rungs are down, and its
  layout (sister | brain, both raw loops) shows nothing an operator can read.

## Deliverables

**A. Capture loop output** — `fleet/watchdog.py` respawns append stdout+stderr to a
per-rung log: `.fleet/brain.log`, `.fleet/sister.log`, `.fleet/monitor.log`
(append mode, line-buffered, created if missing). Existing watchdog tests extended to
cover the log path.

**B. Meaningful brain context** — `fleet/brain.py` prints a low-noise, human-readable
context stream to stdout: a startup status header; on handling an order the order id +
the verbatim task/body received, then `→ dispatched #N at <tier>/<thinking>` or
`→ refused: <reason>`; `→ advanced waves: dispatched [...]`; and an idle heartbeat line
about every 30s (`[brain] idle 30s | orders pending=0 | dispatched=11 | waves: #219=[232]
| claims=0 | HEAD=8d9c219 | watchdog=healthy`). Existing behaviour/tests stay green; a
test asserts the status line contains the expected fields.

**C. Live console dashboard** — new tracked `fleet/console.py`: self-refreshing dashboard
(clear + redraw ~4s) with header (repo, HEAD, time), rungs (pid/state/commit/beat age),
orders (pending + latest operator order), dispatches (latest brain acks), live claims,
wave progress (parent + children with glyphs closed ✓ / dispatched ▶ / pending ·), recent
events (last ~8 `slog.jsonl`, truncated), watchdog (last ~5 `.fleet/watchdog.log` lines).
`--once` renders once and exits; clean exit on Ctrl-C/SIGTERM. Rendering lives in pure
helper functions so tests assert output without a TTY; `fleet/tests/test_console.py`.

**D. Log into the live session** — `fleet/control.py` gains a `live` verb (alias
`attach`): ensure the rungs are running (reuse the existing start logic), create/reuse a
tmux session named `fleet` laid out as a `dashboard` window (`python3 fleet/console.py`)
plus `brain` and `sister` windows (`tail -f .fleet/<rung>.log`), then attach and print
`attaching to the live fleet session — detach with Ctrl-b d`. Dry-run/print mode so the
tmux command construction is unit-testable (tmux `attach` must never run in tests).
`fleet/run-fleet.sh` uses the same layout and never kills a healthy fleet. A "Log into the
live session" section is added to `fleet/README.md`.

## Why now

The brain is the middle rung of the hierarchy (M26, epic #160) and it is currently
unobservable: its output is discarded by the watchdog, it says nothing on startup or while
idle, and no session exists to attach to. An operator who cannot see the brain cannot tell
a working fleet from a wedged one.

## Facts the implementation must respect

- The brain prints to stdout; the log is written by the **watchdog** at spawn time, so the
  two must agree on the path (`.fleet/<rung>.log`).
- `run-fleet.sh` is guard-aware: the singleton locks refuse a blind recreate, so the tmux
  layout must be created **only** for missing rungs and must attach (never kill) when the
  session already exists.

## Verify

```bash
set -o pipefail; python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "PYTEST RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
make verify
```

Both must be green, reported with actual output.

## Operator command (after merge)

```bash
python3 fleet/control.py live
```

items.title: [fleet-task] Institutional lane isolation: session identity minted per issue, own worktree, own commit signature
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
**GOAL — institutional lane isolation.** Every fleet agent session runs as a uniquely minted identity bound to its GitHub issue, in its own `git worktree` on a branch named for that issue, and every commit it makes carries that session's signature — so a commit's authorship *and* its worktree both point back at exactly one ticket, and breaking the rule fails `make verify`.

An agent session becomes a first-class identity. The loop mints a `session_id` for
the issue, provisions a dedicated worktree on branch `issue-<n>` off
`origin/master`, writes the session's git author/committer identity into that
worktree's **own** config (never the shared repo config, so lane A cannot sign as
lane B), and exports the identity into the agent's environment before it starts.
Isolation stops being a convention an agent is asked to honour and becomes a
state the machine establishes and a gate re-checks.

Role: subagent
Epic: #160
Pillar: autonomous-ops
Lane: governance-isolation
Model tier (FinOps): pro
Thinking effort: medium
Verify: `make verify`

Chain markers:

    Parent: #160
    Part-of: #160
    Blocked-by: none

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `governance/isolation/` mints a `SessionIdentity` from an issue number and agent id: unique `session_id`, canonical branch `issue-<n>`, worktree path, and the git author/committer signature (`agent-<id> <agent+<id>@...>`) — deterministic for the same mint inputs (`pytest governance/isolation/tests`).
- [ ] Provisioning a lane creates a real worktree on `issue-<n>` from `origin/master` and writes the identity with `git config --worktree`, so two lanes on one machine hold two different commit signatures at the same time (proved by a two-lane test).
- [ ] The session exports `AO_SESSION_ID`, `AO_ISSUE`, `AO_AGENT_ID`, `AO_LANE`, `AO_BRANCH`, `AO_WORKTREE`, `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` (`session env`), and `fleet/terminal.py` uses them for every spawn.
- [ ] `session audit` refuses a lane whose branch does not encode its issue, whose git identity is not the session's signature, or whose commits lack the `Refs kushin77/agent-orchestrator#<n>` trailer.
- [ ] `scripts/check-session-isolation.sh` runs a live mint -> provision -> commit -> audit round trip and **fails** on each mutated input (wrong branch, human identity, missing trailer, identity leaked into the shared config) — wired into `make verify`, since a check that cannot fail is a formality.
- [ ] The rule is declared institutionally in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md` and `docs/GOVERNANCE.md`, and the gate fails if any of those declarations is removed.

Evidence

    (paste the real `make verify` output here)

items.title: Attach the operator's enterprise instruction stack to fleet directives (brain KB)
items.body:
## Summary

Give the fleet's dispatched subagents the SAME enterprise instruction stack the
operator's top-level agent runs under — the DeepSeek module, the CMR module, and
all module instruction files — for full enterprise connection.

## Problem

`fleet/brain.py` attaches a KB to every directive via
`KB_SOURCES = tuple(PROFILE["kb"]["fleet_modules"])` and `build_directive`
renders a "Read first (fleet KB)" block. Today
`fleet/profiles/brain.profile.json` `kb` carries:

- `own_repo` — relative repo docs (loadable), and
- `fleet_modules` — descriptive STRINGS ("kushin77/deepseek — fleet/SME/..."),
  NOT loadable file paths.

So the subagents never actually read the doctrine the operator's top-level
agent runs under.

## Change

1. Add `kb.enterprise_instructions` to `fleet/profiles/brain.profile.json`
   holding the operator's instruction stack (home-relative, `~` prefix):
   `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/rules/context7.md`, the VS Code user
   prompts, `~/deepseek/{AGENTS,CLAUDE}.md`, `~/cmr/{AGENTS,GOLDEN-RULES}.md`,
   `~/cmr/docs/*.md` key docs, and all 11 `~/.copilot/agents/*.agent.md` SME
   profiles. Keep `own_repo` and `fleet_modules` intact (profile gate).
2. In `fleet/brain.py`, expand `~` (`Path(source).expanduser()`) when building
   the KB list and combine `own_repo` + `enterprise_instructions` (+ keep the
   module pointers) in the "Read first" block, so it reads as loadable paths.
3. Update `fleet/tests/test_brain.py` (and any KB/profile test) to match; add a
   test asserting the directive carries the enterprise instruction paths.
4. Note the enterprise instruction stack in `fleet/README.md`.

## Files

- fleet/profiles/brain.profile.json
- fleet/brain.py
- fleet/tests/test_brain.py
- fleet/README.md

## Verify

```
set -o pipefail; python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "PYTEST RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
make verify
```

items.title: Track the fleet progress monitor as a third watchdog rung (durable, auto-start)
items.body:
## Goal
Make the fleet task-progress monitor a durable, TRACKED component of the fleet that auto-starts and self-heals, owned by the existing cron watchdog.

## Context
There is currently a runtime-only watcher at `.fleet/open-eye.sh` (gitignored, ad-hoc). It polls every 20s and writes a change-only line to `.fleet/open-eye.log` and a liveness line to `.fleet/open-eye.heartbeat`. It reads sister/brain state, held claims, the wave dispatch list, and git HEAD.

The cron-owned watchdog `fleet/watchdog.py` currently ensures only brain and sister stay alive.

## Change
1. Add a tracked `fleet/monitor.py` implementing the same change-only polling (sister/brain state, held claims, wave dispatch list, git HEAD), writing to `.fleet/open-eye.log` (change-only, timestamped) and `.fleet/open-eye.heartbeat` (liveness), sleeping ~20s, exiting cleanly on SIGTERM. Runtime output stays under gitignored `.fleet/`.
2. Add the monitor as a third rung in `fleet/watchdog.py` so a missing monitor process is respawned on the cron tick (simple process-presence check via `pgrep -f fleet/monitor.py`).
3. Update `fleet/tests/test_watchdog.py` and add a short fleet-monitor section to `fleet/README.md`.

## Verify
- `set -o pipefail; python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "PYTEST RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"`
- `make verify`

items.title: fleet: subagent prompt must merge its own green PR and close the issue
items.body:
## Problem

`fleet/terminal.py` `build_prompt` instructs the spawned subagent to "open a PR" but **never to merge it**. Consequences:

- A finished issue's work sits as an open PR forever (e.g. #232 → PR #236), never merged.
- A re-dispatch that finds an existing open PR bails out with "#232 already done, PR open", leaving the issue open.

## Required change

In `fleet/terminal.py` `build_prompt`, add explicit subagent instructions:

1. After `make verify` is green and the PR is open, squash-merge it (`gh pr merge <number> --squash --delete-branch`) and close the issue — **never** leave a completed PR unmerged.
2. If a PR for the issue **already exists**, fetch + check out its branch, run `make verify`, and if green **merge it** and close the issue — do **not** bail out leaving the issue open.
3. The returned report must include the merge result (PR number + merged/closed).

Also update `fleet/profiles/brain.profile.json` `templates.report` to carry the same merge mandate (it is appended to every directive body by `fleet/brain.py` `build_directive`).

Update `fleet/tests/test_terminal.py` to match, adding a test that asserts the prompt mandates merge + already-done handling.

## Verify

- `set -o pipefail; python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "PYTEST RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"`
- `make verify`

items.title: Sync waves with the deepseek and code-indexing modules: bidirectional capability feedback loop
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
Parent: #160

Blocked-by: #180

## Summary
Perfect sync with `kushin77/deepseek` and `kushin77/code-indexing` — their
maturity has a long way to go, so their enhancements must flow into every
consecutive wave of THIS repo, and each wave must get faster / cheaper /
smarter as a result. This issue is the sync contract plus the gap register:
what the owner's intent implies that is not yet built.

## Ground truth (2026-09-13)

**Their boards already point at us:**
- code-indexing #130 — "agent-orchestrator's engine/memory/prompt_cache.py
  re-derives the static-first/delta-last discipline instead of consuming codeidx
  context-pack".
- code-indexing #129 — "agent-orchestrator's MCP gateway re-implements codeidx
  tool *shapes* as fake data, never queries the real indexer".
- code-indexing #128 — "publish a stable consumption contract for codeidx
  context-pack so external repos can integrate".
- code-indexing #132 — DR-069 measurement artifact (0.0105ms L1 / 63.2%→80-92%
  L2 prompt-cache baselines) — the numbers every wave's FinOps must cite.
- deepseek #91/#88-90 — steer-dispatch and Claude-CLI-on-DeepSeek BYOK — the
  same steering problem our brain/sister model solves, for another runtime.
- deepseek #84/#79 — auto-file lessons as issues and keep the board in sync;
  feed lessons back via dispatch hints.
- deepseek #74 — pmo start-to-finish board sequencing (overlaps our
  chronological dispatch doctrine).

**Our current indexer is repo-local** (`governance/knowledge/README.md`): it
indexes this repository's artefacts, not the fleet's boards, and it does not
consume the codeidx context-pack.

## The sync contract (what each wave must do)

1. **Wave bootstrap = a query, not memory.** Each wave starts by running a
   code-native report: what merged/opened in deepseek + code-indexing since the
   last wave, plus the codeidx context-pack deltas. The report is an artefact,
   not a conversation.
2. **Consume, don't re-implement.** Any indexing/prompt-cache/tool-shape work in
   our waves must consume the codeidx context-pack (#128) and cite DR-069
   baselines (#132). Re-derivation is a conformance failure.
3. **Push back.** Every wave closes with direction issues to their boards for
   what the NEXT wave needs (the bidirectional half of "perfect sync").
4. **Pin for reproducibility.** Each wave pins the SHAs of the deepseek module
   and codeidx context-pack it consumed (GR-10 provenance).
5. **Gate on health, don't wait on maturity.** The module health gate (#122)
   is a wave precondition that degrades the wave scope — a missing enhancement
   becomes a deferred, flag-gated item plus a direction issue, never a blocked
   wave.
6. **Measure the loop.** Waves get a ledger: duration, cost per issue, model
   escalations, verify-fail rate — so "faster/cheaper/smarter" is provable,
   not asserted. deepseek's metering must be truthful first (their #115).

## What the owner's intent is missing (gap register)

| # | Gap | Owning issue |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cross-repo chain edges — our `Blocked-by:` parser only understands same-repo issue numbers; `Blocked-by: kushin77/code-indexing#128` must parse and gate | this issue |
| 2 | Wave-bootstrap report (the delta query) — code, not prose | this issue |
| 3 | Wave ledger + SLOs (duration/cost/escalations/verify-rate per wave) | this issue |
| 4 | Codeidx context-pack consumption contract in our engine/memory (#129/#130) | direction to our board |
| 5 | Steering contract unification — brain/sister vs deepseek steer-dispatch (#91) must be ONE contract across runtimes | #161 |
| 6 | Lessons-loop sync — deepseek #84/#79 and our #141 must share one ledger, not two | #141 |
| 7 | Board-sequencing doctrine sync — deepseek #74 vs our dispatch rules must agree | CMR#992 |
| 8 | Fleet worktree policy — code-indexing #158/#159 flag /tmp (tmpfs) worktrees as an inode/RAM hazard on the shared workstation; our waves must stop using /tmp worktrees | this issue |
| 9 | Wave triage lane — a standing lane that reviews their boards each wave and files direction issues (bidirectional sync needs an owner) | this issue |
| 10 | Trusted feed — their enhancements enter our waves only via reviewed direction/harvest issues with provenance; no silent adoption | this issue |

## Verify
```bash
make verify
python3 governance/knowledge/cli.py validate
```

## Related
- #139 (indexer), #122 (module health gate), #180 (lessons register),
  #161/#163/#164 (the current wave), CMR#992 (GR-20b), code-indexing #128/#129/
  #130/#132, deepseek #74/#79/#84/#91/#115

items.title: Lessons from first live steering + enterprise-scale hardening register
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
Parent: #160

## Summary
Lessons from taking the session-fleet A2A model live, and the register of what a
true elite / SaaS / enterprise-scale version still needs. Filed now, while the
first live steering is fresh — this issue is the input for the #141 RCA/lessons
enforcement once that gate lands.

## Lessons learned (the file-mailbox + push/wait/trigger decision)

1. **A dumb terminal needs a pulse.** Transport is not a loop: the first live
   steering deadlocked for 140 s with two directives queued because the sister
   had no listener (#175). Lesson: ship the listener with the transport, and
   test the *loop*, not the channel.
2. **Consume-on-report keeps the queue honest.** Answered directives left in the
   inbox look like outstanding work; `report` must retire what it answers.
3. **Every pair of enforcement surfaces needs an explicit edge.** The channel
   directs; the claim gate refuses — the `claim --directive` integration (#178)
   is the bridge. Any future enforcement pair needs its bridge designed, not
   discovered.
4. **Declared is not verified.** The sister's runtime mode (DSv4FNone) has no
   introspection surface; the runbook needs a runtime attestation artifact
   (#166 comment).
5. **Shared temp paths and shared gate files collide.** Two sessions derived the
   same worktree path; two lanes adding gates to Makefile/verify.sh conflict.
   Unique worktree names + explicit `git add` + keep-both merge resolution.
6. **The cheapest capable tier was right.** flash/none steered the sister through
   a real bootstrap with zero escalations.

## What enterprise scale still needs (register)

- **Transport promotion** — the file mailbox is single-host localhost mechanics
  (GR-21). Multi-host/SaaS needs the M9 A2A layer (HTTP/SSE + Agent Cards,
  #102–#109).
- **Trust** — signed, authenticated directives; the mailbox trusts the
  filesystem (M9 #106).
- **Brain supervision** — no brain-side daemon, latching alerts, or escalation
  path when a directive stalls; today the brain polls.
- **Queue QoS** — priorities, deadlines, retries/backoff, per-directive budget
  caps (partially #164).
- **Observability** — correlation ids exist but nothing aggregates latency/cost
  per directive chain (M9 #107).
- **Tenant isolation** — one repo = one org today; the product's identity pillar
  must scope fleets per tenant.
- **Durable brain** — the brain is a single session; enterprise needs a durable
  orchestrator + state machine (leaderboard's orchestrator pattern, M9 #105).

## Verify
None (register only) — but every item above must end up tracked in its owning
issue before M26 closes.

## Related
- #175 (listener), #178 (brain-directed claims), #166 (runtime attestation gap)

items.title: Close the steering loop: sister-side listener (watch) + consume-on-report
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
Parent: #160

Blocked-by: #171

## Summary
Steering broke on first contact with a live sister session: the brain pushed the
work directive for #141, blocked on `wait`, and **timed out after 140 s with
`inbox: 2 pending`** — the sister had no listener, so queued directives sat
unread. A push/wait trigger is only half a loop without a sister-side pulse.

## Scope
- `fleet/channel.py watch` (sister side): return the oldest pending directive,
  or block until one arrives. Exit 0 = directive returned, 1 = IDLE (nothing in
  the window; run it again), 2 = CANNOT-ASSESS (inbox unreadable).
- Consume-on-report: answering a directive moves it from `.fleet/inbox` to
  `.fleet/done`, so the pending count is the number of outstanding orders
  instead of a growing pile of already-answered orders.
- `.fleet/done/` added to the ignore list; README documents the listener loop.

## Acceptance criteria
- A queued directive is returned by `watch` immediately; an empty inbox reports
  IDLE (rc=1) rather than blocking forever.
- Reporting consumes the directive it answers; consuming an absent directive is
  a no-op, not an error.
- The gate stays green and the new paths are covered by tests.

## Verify
```bash
python3 -m pytest fleet/tests -q
bash scripts/check-fleet-channel.sh
make verify
```

## Evidence that this is real
Timed-out brain wait (rc=1) with two pending directives, while the sister
reported itself "idling, awaiting next directive" — the missing piece was the
listener, not the transport.

items.body:
Parent: #160

## Summary

Six issues declare a class whose expectations they do not meet, surfaced by the
conformance checker delivered in #140. Each is a declared-vs-actual mismatch: the
class on the issue promises more than the issue's own metadata shows.

Measured from the committed board snapshot (`.board/snapshot.json`), milestoned open
issues only:

| Issue | Declared class | Missing | Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| #143 | `elite` | `pillar:` | M24 |
| #150 | `elite` | `pillar:` | M25 |
| #163 | `enterprise` | `gdc:` | M26 |
| #164 | `enterprise` | `gdc:` | M26 |
| #165 | `enterprise` | `gdc:` | M26 |
| #166 | `elite` | `gdc:` | M26 |

Reproduce with:

```bash
python3 governance/conformance/cli.py check
# WARNING class-expectation-unmet  issue #143 is class 'elite', which expects a `pillar:` label
# ... six findings, plus the un-milestoned scope note
```

## Why these are deviations rather than errors

The checker treats them as warnings so the gate is not red for reasons a single lane
cannot fix by working its own issue. Enforcement covers what a lane controls
(classification present, class on the ladder, one class per issue, companion labels),
and the per-class expectations are reported. Once these six are resolved,
`--strict` can be enabled for the affected milestones:

```bash
python3 governance/conformance/cli.py check --milestone "M24 - ..." --strict
```

## Required corrective action

For each issue, either:

1. **Add the missing label** — `pillar:<value>` for #143/#150, `gdc:enterprise` for
   #163–#166 — when the class genuinely describes the work; or
2. **Lower the declared class** to the rung the work actually meets (e.g.
   `class:pattern` instead of `class:enterprise`).

Option 1 is expected for all six: the work is program-level, and the only gap is the
label. #138 (the M24 epic) and #160–#167 carry both labels, so the vocabulary and the
convention already exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- All six issues carry the expected label, or their class is lowered to match.
- `python3 governance/conformance/cli.py check` reports zero deviations for
  milestoned issues.
- `--strict` passes for M24, M25 and M26.
- `make verify` stays green.

Refs #140 (checker), parent #138

items.title: Harden the claim gate: snapshot staleness check + conflict-free claim storage
items.body:
## Summary

Two defects in the claim gate (`governance/dispatch`, merged in #159). Both were
observed directly while using the gate to pick up the next issue, and both can
cause the wrong outcome for the agents the gate is meant to steer.

## Defect 1 — the snapshot has no freshness check, so the gate can name a closed issue

`.board/snapshot.json` is a tracked artifact refreshed only by an explicit command.
Nothing records or enforces how old it is, so the gate answers confidently from
stale data.

Observed 2026-09-13:

```
$ python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py status
snapshot: kushin77/agent-orchestrator generated 2026-09-13T17:46:59Z (105 issues)
active milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
frontier: #139 Implement the CMR/GDC institutional knowledge indexer
```

`#139` had already been **closed** at `18:02:43Z`. The snapshot was 19 minutes old
and the gate still presented a closed issue as the eligible frontier, with no
staleness signal in the output. Only an explicit refresh corrected it:

```
$ python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py snapshot --from-github
snapshot: wrote .board/snapshot.json (113 issues, 13 with declared chain edges)

$ python3 governance/dispatch/cli.py status
snapshot: kushin77/agent-orchestrator generated 2026-09-13T18:06:16Z (113 issues)
frontier: #140 Enforce CMR class, pattern, and template conformance across repos
```

This matters because `eligible` is what an agent acts on. A stale frontier either
sends an agent at finished work, or, worse, refuses a legitimate claim as
out-of-order.

**Proposed:** record `generated_at` age and fail closed past a threshold —
`eligible`/`status` should emit `CANNOT-ASSESS` (exit 2) rather than a verdict when
the snapshot is older than N minutes, and the age should be printed on every run.

## Defect 2 — the claim ledger is one tracked file, so concurrent lanes collide

`.board/claims.jsonl` is a single append-only file under version control
(`DEFAULT_LEDGER` in `governance/dispatch/claims.py`). Every lane that claims an
issue writes to that same path, which makes a conflict structural rather than
occasional.

Observed 2026-09-13, while lane `#162` was in flight:

```
$ git -C /tmp/ao162-copilot status --short
A  .board/claims.jsonl
UU Makefile
A  governance/knowledge/README.md
...
```

That worktree was mid-merge with an unresolved conflict, with `.board/claims.jsonl`
staged as an addition — while the main checkout separately carried local
modifications to the same tracked file. Two consequences:

1. **Merge conflicts on every concurrent pair of lanes.** A ledger line is
   append-only, but git sees a whole-file change.
2. **A claim can be lost.** A conflict resolved by taking one side silently drops
   the other lane's claim — the exact failure the ledger exists to prevent, now
   caused by the ledger itself.

Related: because the ledger is tracked, a local modification to it blocks
`git pull --ff-only` with "untracked working tree files would be overwritten", so
lanes that copy the ledger into their own worktree must remove the original in the
main checkout before syncing.

**Proposed:** one file per claim, e.g. `.board/claims/<issue>-<agent>.json`, so
concurrent lanes touch disjoint paths and a conflict is impossible by construction.
The audit already reads a directory-shaped claim set in the earlier design sketch,
and replay over sorted files is deterministic.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed here

Fixing either changes the gate's public contract (`CANNOT-ASSESS` semantics;
ledger path and replay), which is #159's lane. This issue records the evidence and
the proposed direction so the decision is explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

- Snapshot staleness is detected and surfaced on every `status`/`eligible` run.
- A snapshot past the threshold yields `CANNOT-ASSESS` (exit 2), never a verdict.
- Claims are stored so that two concurrent lanes cannot conflict on one path.
- A lost-claim scenario is covered by a negative-control test.
- The tri-state exit-code contract is preserved and documented.

verdict (GR-10 provenance); (2) reuse the mature vocabulary — do not invent a
parallel taxonomy; (3) where the mature shape is bash/GitHub-bound, take the
PATTERN and re-implement for this repo, saying so in the PR.

## Never-idle dispatcher spec (owner directive, 2026-09-13)

The dispatcher is the loop that must **never idle** and **always watch** the
inbox — and every message must be **tied to a GitHub issue**:

1. **Persistent loop** — `while True` with `--interval <s>` polling. Unlike
   `watch`, it never exits on IDLE; an empty inbox is just another poll cycle.
   `--max-iterations` and `--once` exist for tests only.
2. **Every executable message names an issue** — a directive without
   `task.issue` is refused and reported (a message that names no issue is not
   work). This is the tie to GitHub issues.
3. **Code-native runner** — spawn the subagent headless:
   `claude -p "<prompt>"` (confirmed `-p/--print` on this machine) by default,
   overridable with `--runner` (e.g. `deepseek …` once its headless flag is
   known — deepseek #91). `--dry-run` prints the exact command without running.
4. **Prompt template** — the subagent prompt carries: the issue, "claim with
   `--directive <id>`", the harvest-first sources, "PR `Closes #<n>`", "paste
   the ACTUAL `make verify` output", and "report back".
5. **Report on completion** — `fleet/channel.py report --from sister
   --correlation <directive id> --type result` (consumes the directive).
6. **Stop conditions** — a `halt` directive or SIGINT/SIGTERM; anything else
   keeps looping (a failing directive is reported and the loop continues).
7. **Heartbeat** — one log line per poll so "never idle" is observable, not
   assumed (declared-not-verified is a known gap, #166).

**Why:** the sister's turn-based loop completed #141, #161 and spawned #163,
then idled with #164/#165/#166 unclaimed — the loop must not depend on a chat
session remembering to re-run `watch`. This dispatcher removes that dependency.
