items.title: EPIC: Session Fleet Operating Model — Brain / Fleet Brain / Epic Subagent Fleet (e2e IT department)
items.milestone: M26 - Session Fleet Operating Model (Brain / Fleet Brain / Subagents)
items.body:
# EPIC — Session Fleet Operating Model (owner intent, 2026-09-13)

> The purpose of this repo: **the complete end-to-end IT department for any
> organization, Enterprise or SaaS** — work intake, dispatch, execution,
> verification, merge, observability, FinOps and governance, run by agents.
> It is close to that today; this epic closes the session-operations gap.

## Charter — the owner's operating model, preserved verbatim

1. We use DeepSeek in Copilot.
2. Two sessions: (a) the **Brain** — this session; (b) the **Fleet Brain** —
   the sister session.
3. The Brain sends commands to the sister session.
4. The sister session runs **DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, no thinking effort**.
5. The sister acts as a **dumb terminal** taking orders from the Brain.
6. The sister spawns **epic-focused fleet subagents**, directed by the Brain,
   using DeepSeek agent-model **FinOps controls** to choose the proper model
   and thinking level (pro vs flash) — while the GitHub issue template is
   enhanced to be conscious of this intended behaviour.
7. Brain ↔ sister and sister ↔ subagents communicate over **A2A** — or
   whichever pattern is elite and best practice; the Brain (steered by the
   advisor with max DeepSeek vPro) decides and documents it.
8. The advisor documents the entire intent as project / milestone / epic /
   issues.
9. **The single human bootstrap:** put the sister session into **DSv4FNone**
   mode. Everything after that is code.

## What this epic owns

- The session topology and the steering contract (who may tell whom what).
- The steering channel: message schema, mailbox, channel CLI, loop runner.
- The fleet-brain dispatcher: a dumb-terminal executor that only does what a
  directive says — spawn epic-focused subagents with per-task FinOps
  directives; reject anything outside the whitelist.
- The FinOps model chooser for fleet subagents (model tier + thinking effort,
  pro vs flash), enforced, not advisory.
- The GitHub issue template enhancement carrying the intended behaviour
  (role, epic focus, model tier, thinking effort, brain directive, verify,
  lane).
- The session bootstrap + runbook (zero-touch beyond the model switch).
- The e2e pilot and its negative controls.

## Non-goals

- Not a tenant-facing product feature yet; this is how THIS repo is operated.
- The hub's A2A product layer (M9, #101–#109) is the platform contract this
  model consumes; this epic does not rebuild it.

## Acceptance criteria (epic level)

- One brain directive flows brain → sister → subagent → PR → merge with
  evidence, with zero human steps after the DSv4FNone switch.
- Every step of the flow is enforceable: a forged, out-of-order or
  over-privileged directive is refused with a real failing check.
- The issue template renders this operating model on every issue created.

## Verify

```bash
make verify
make gate
```

## Chain

The child issues below are the implementation sequence (milestone M26).

items.title: Enforce issue order at claim time (behavioral, not just declared): eligibility check + single-claim lock
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
## Summary
The `chronological-dispatch` gate (`scripts/check-chronological-dispatch.sh`) is a **declaration gate**: it fails when `AGENTS.md`, `docs/GOVERNANCE.md`, or `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md` stop declaring dependency-ordered selection. It does **not** stop an agent from claiming an out-of-order issue — which is the actual failure the owner reported ("not working in this repo in my other session").

This issue tracks the behavioral half: enforce order at **claim time**.

## Gap
- Nothing validates that a claimed issue is the next eligible step in the active chain (blocker of an open issue / next milestone item / child required to close an open parent).
- Nothing prevents two agents claiming the same issue or the same defect — observed on 2026-09-13: PR #155 and PR #156 shipped identical fixes for #154 concurrently, and the second merge was wasted work.
- The board still looks like a browsable backlog to a claiming agent.

## Proposed mechanism (declarative where possible, IaC-first)
1. **Claim record** — an issue claim is written as a tracked artifact (e.g. `.board/claims/<issue>.json` via the ops runner) carrying agent id, lane, base commit, and timestamp.
2. **Eligibility check** — the claim is rejected unless the issue is reachable from the active chain: parent/child edge, milestone/phase position, or explicit blocker relation.
3. **Single-claim lock** — a second claim on an in-flight issue fails loudly (no silent double lane).
4. **Gate wiring** — the eligibility check runs in the dispatch path (and, where it can be evaluated statically, as a `make verify` check), with real failure paths (no false green).
5. **No human step** — the claim/lock and the checks are code + repo artifacts; nothing requires operator action.

## Acceptance criteria
- Claiming an issue that is not the next eligible step in the active chain fails with a message naming the issue, the active chain, and the missing edge.
- A second concurrent claim on an in-flight issue fails.
- The mechanism is exercised by a negative-control test that proves both failures.
- The check is green from a clean checkout of `master` (prove against the committed tree, not a dirty working tree — the trap hit in #154).
- No doc-only rule is introduced (GR-29): the rule is only binding where the check can fail.

## Verify
```bash
make verify
# negative control: out-of-order claim must fail; duplicate claim must fail
```

## Related
- #152 / PR #153 (rule + declaration gate), #154 / PR #155 (clean-checkout false-green fix)
- `kushin77/CMR#992` (GR-20b direction: hub rule, hub gate, instruction layer, fleet rollout)
- Lane ownership: one issue = one lane = one branch (`docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md`)

## Chain

Parent: #144

items.title: Chronological-dispatch gate is red on a clean checkout: contract docs were never committed (#152)
items.body:
## Summary
The `chronological-dispatch` gate merged in PR #153 is **red on a clean checkout** of `master` (`6dc8fd2`). It passes only because the three contract documents it validates exist as **uncommitted local edits** in one working tree. Any fresh clone, CI runner, or agent checkout reads a red gate — i.e. the enforcement landed without the rule it enforces.

## Reproduction (proven, on `6dc8fd2`)
```bash
d="$(mktemp -d /tmp/chrono-clean.XXXXXX)"; mkdir -p "$d/scripts" "$d/docs"
git show 6dc8fd2:AGENTS.md                > "$d/AGENTS.md"
git show 6dc8fd2:docs/GOVERNANCE.md       > "$d/docs/GOVERNANCE.md"
git show 6dc8fd2:docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md   > "$d/docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md"
cp scripts/check-chronological-dispatch.sh "$d/scripts/"
bash "$d/scripts/check-chronological-dispatch.sh"
```
Actual output:
```
  FAIL  AGENTS.md (missing rule marker: chronological)
  FAIL  AGENTS.md (missing rule marker: dependency)
  FAIL  AGENTS.md (missing rule marker: Kanban)
  FAIL  docs/GOVERNANCE.md (missing rule marker: chronological)
  FAIL  docs/GOVERNANCE.md (missing rule marker: dependency)
  FAIL  docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md (missing rule marker: chronological)
  FAIL  docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md (missing rule marker: dependency)
chronological-dispatch: FAIL (3 of 3 contract doc(s) non-conforming)
CLEAN-CHECKOUT rc=1
```

## Impact
- **False-green in the working tree only.** `make verify` reports `PASS (9 of 9)` locally purely because of uncommitted edits — the exact failure mode GR-12 forbids.
- Issue #152 was closed by PR #153 while its own acceptance criterion ("repo documentation must declare the rule in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/GOVERNANCE.md`, `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md`") is unmet in the committed tree.
- Any agent that reads the rule from a fresh checkout (the enterprise-wide audience for this rule) gets nothing.

## Fix
Commit the three contract documents that declare the rule:
- `AGENTS.md` — golden rule: chronological, dependency-gated issue selection (no kanban scavenging).
- `docs/GOVERNANCE.md` — § Chronological issue dispatch (mandatory).
- `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md` — chronological dispatch rule in the dispatch contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- `bash scripts/check-chronological-dispatch.sh` passes against the **committed** tree, not the working tree.
- `make verify` is green from a clean checkout of `master`.
- No uncommitted dependency remains for a green gate.

## Verify
```bash
bash scripts/check-chronological-dispatch.sh   # must exit 0 from a clean checkout
make verify                                    # must be green
```

## Related
- #152 (rule + acceptance criteria; closed by #153 before the docs landed)
- PR #153 (the gate itself)

items.title: Enforce chronological issue dispatch across all agents
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
## Summary
All agents across the enterprise must consume GitHub work in dependency-order, end-to-end sequence, not by ad hoc board scavenging or kanban picking.

## Rule
- No agent may pick a GitHub issue solely because it is visible on the board.
- The next valid issue is the next step in the current milestone / phase / parent-child chain.
- A child issue is only eligible when it is required to close the currently active issue or advance the current dependency chain.
- Unrelated board items remain queued until the active chain reaches them.
- Kanban drift is a governance violation.

## Why this matters
DeepSeek started this pattern, but it is not reliably enforced in the repo and can silently become issue-scavenging. This must become a hard execution rule across all agents, not a recommendation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Repo governance docs define chronological issue selection as mandatory.
- Agents are blocked from selecting unrelated board items while a dependency chain is active.

items.title: Provide the enterprise/GDC roll-up — tenant hierarchy and org aggregate view
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
Parent: #144

## Summary

Provide the **enterprise/org/GDC roll-up**: a tenant hierarchy and org-level aggregate view where every repo's per-repo fleet ("personal CTO engineering team") reports up to a single enterprise control plane.

## Cannibalization sources

- `kushin77/CMR/catalog/sme-registry.tsv` — per-SME weekly_spend_ceiling (the FinOps roll-up primitive).
- `kushin77/CMR/onboarding/agent-profiles/persona-registry.json` — unified persona registry linking cards/profiles/lanes.
- `kushin77/leaderboard/scripts/data/fleet-metrics-per-model.sh` — per-model invocation/success/failure/cost leaderboard.
- `kushin77/agent-orchestrator/registry/personas/persona-card.schema.json` — `tenant` field with platform fallback (the tenant-hierarchy seed).

## Acceptance criteria

- Repos/modules roll up under tenants, which roll up under the enterprise/GDC org.
- An org-level view aggregates per-repo fleets: which SMEs exist, utilization, spend vs ceiling, closure rate, drift.
- Per-repo fleets remain isolated beneath the roll-up (the enterprise view is a projection, never a second source of truth).
- Roll-up metrics are computed, not narrated, and are gate-verified.

## Definition of done

- Tenant hierarchy + org aggregate view implemented for the pilot repos.
- Per-repo isolation holds while the enterprise view is live.
- `make verify` green.

items.title: Enforce repo separation, admin rights, and end-to-end issue closure
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
Parent: #144

## Summary

Enforce **repo separation, admin rights, and end-to-end issue closure** so each repo's fleet is its own personal CTO engineering team that controls, locks, and implements its issues to full closure under scoped admin authority — while every repo stays isolated from every other repo.

## Cannibalization sources

- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/docs/wiki/ELITE_COMMANDER_LTC_CHARTER.md` — Commander (brain, no execution, only role with merge authority) + Lieutenant-Commander (execution arm) split.
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/docs/wiki/ELITE_GENERAL_CHARTER.md`, `ELITE_PLATOON_LEADER_CHARTER.md`, `ELITE_AUDITOR_CHARTER.md`, `ELITE_SCRIBE_CHARTER.md` — chain-of-command with per-role authority and separation of duties.
- `kushin77/leaderboard/docs/LEADERBOARD_PROTOCOL.md` — worktree-per-session isolation (collision→isolation).
- `kushin77/agent-orchestrator/registry/personas/persona-card.schema.json` — `posture: executor|reviewer|auditor` (an auditor can never execute what it audits).

## Acceptance criteria

- Repo-level admin rights are scoped to that repo's fleet; no fleet can act on another repo's files, issues, or state.
- A single enterprise-level controller has full admin across repos for roll-up, but is the only cross-repo actor.
- End-to-end closure is enforced: an issue is only "done" when the fleet's own gate AND the repo's `make verify` pass with recorded output (never merge failing work).
- Separation of duties is schema-enforced (executor ≠ reviewer ≠ auditor for the same work item).

## Definition of done

- Two repos' fleets demonstrated to be fully isolated (no shared state, no cross-repo writes).
- Admin-rights matrix documented and enforced.
- End-to-end closure gated on real verification evidence.
- `make verify` green.

items.title: Port SME-squad routing + capability/route/tier FinOps configs into the gateway
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
Parent: #144

## Summary

Port the **SME-squad routing + capability/route/tier FinOps configs** into the gateway and queue layers: which SME handles which domain, which fleet carries which role, and how complexity/risk routes to a model tier with cost controls.

## Cannibalization sources

- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/config/leaderboard/capability-registry.json` — agent roles (planner/executor/verifier/critic) + worker fleets (text/shell/code/scout/scribe/auditor) with access levels + dispatch chains.
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/config/leaderboard/route-policy.json` — complexity/risk → chain + tier (fast/deep/strict) with keyword thresholds.
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/config/leaderboard/tier-policy.json` — model tiers (flash/pro/auditor) with timeouts, token caps, fallbacks, complexity→tier map.
- `kushin77/leaderboard/scripts/dispatch/sme-squad-router.sh` + `capital-underwriting/scripts/agent/sme/sme-dispatch.sh` — DOMAIN→SME routing.
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/config/agent-module-authority.json` — domain→module authority matrix.

## Acceptance criteria

- SME routing and capability/route/tier policies are declared data under a validated schema.
- Complexity/risk keywords route to the correct chain and tier; unknown task types default to the deep path.
- Per-tier timeouts/token caps/fallbacks are enforced at the gateway.
- Escalation terminates at a human/advisor when no higher tier exists.

## Definition of done

- Configs ported with provenance and validated by schema.
- A fast-path, deep-path, and strict-path dispatch are each demonstrated.
- `make verify` green.

items.title: Port the leaderboard coordination protocol into the engine state machine
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
## Summary

Port the **leaderboard coordination protocol** into the `engine/` state machine so multi-agent execution per repo is self-registering, deterministic, and verifiable — the "leaderboard" the coordinator reads to see who exists, who is stale, and what is actually done.

## Cannibalization sources

- `kushin77/leaderboard/docs/LEADERBOARD_PROTOCOL.md` (v2) + `LEADERBOARD_RULES.md` + `LEADERBOARD_RUNBOOK.md` — coordination doctrine (invisibility→self-registration; collision→isolation; report computes, never narrates).
- `kushin77/leaderboard/lib/leaderboard-{registry,report,gate,advise}.sh` — registry rows (`ROLE/ID/SCOPE/ISSUES/STATUS/UPDATED`) + computed status (STALE / CLAIM-MISMATCH / WASTED-EFFORT / N-1-ready).
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/docs/wiki/leaderboard/*` — session heartbeat, worktree-per-issue, zombie sweep, cross-session claims.

## Acceptance criteria

- Engine sessions self-register one record each (no shared mutable table); branch/worktree isolation per issue.
- Status is computed from ground truth (issue state, gate results), never self-narrated.
- CLAIM-MISMATCH (claimed done but issue open) and WASTED-EFFORT (working but issue closed) are detected and surfaced.
- The advisor channel (soldier→commander escalation) is realized.

## Definition of done

- Engine state machine implements registry + computed report.
- A stale-session and a claim-mismatch scenario are reproduced in tests and detected.
- `make verify` green.

items.title: Port the CTO overlay as a per-repo drop-in governance layer
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
Parent: #144

## Summary

Port the **CTO overlay** as a per-repo drop-in governance layer: a `.cto/` directory (or its equivalent in the platform) that gives any repo a 4-layer governance team — Executive / Engineering / DevOps / Support — with a validated config schema and tiered enforcement.

## Cannibalization sources

- `kushin77/leaderboard/docs/CTO_OVERLAY.md` — architecture spec (4 layers, BLOCKING/WARNING, non-negotiable signals).
- `kushin77/leaderboard/.cto/{config.yaml,schema.yaml,orchestrator.yaml}` — config + JSON-Schema + master workflow.
- `kushin77/leaderboard/scripts/cto/{apply-overlay.sh,config-engine.sh,cto-orchestrator.sh}` — bootstrap + severity engine + runnable orchestrator (includes the no-false-green `_verdict` tally fix from #1721).
- `kushin77/leaderboard/docs/DS_CTO_AUTONOMY_PROGRAM.md` — DS-CTO autonomy design (LTC-docker always-on + LTC-claude break-glass).

## Acceptance criteria

- The overlay is a versioned, schema-validated, drop-in artifact for any governed repo.
- The 4 layers each have a real runnable gate (the current upstream `.cto/{executive,engineering,devops,support}/run.sh` are stubs — this issue completes them).
- Every blocking layer genuinely blocks on violation; the `_verdict` tally is preserved (no false-green).
- Non-negotiable signals (shell_syntax, secret_scan, protected_files, path_integrity) always run regardless of tier.

## Definition of done

- A repo can apply the overlay and receive a truthful pass/fail report.
- Blocking-fail and warning-only paths both demonstrated.
- `make verify` green; overlay schema validated.

items.title: Ship the per-repo agent fleet template (fleet-composition-as-template)
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
Parent: #144

## Summary

Generalize the fleet-composition machinery into a **per-repo agent fleet template**: every repo/module can instantiate its own SME-focused fleet ("personal CTO engineering team") from a template, without hand-writing profiles.

## Cannibalization sources

- `kushin77/leaderboard/docker/worker-fleet/personas.yaml` + `config/platoons.yaml` — fleet composition + lens→fleet→parallelism routing.
- `kushin77/leaderboard/lib/fleet-roster.sh` — role→model roster as the fleet's single source of truth.
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/infra/docker/worker-fleet/personas.yaml` + `fleet-roster.conf` — 30-persona fleet + definition-vs-run-state split.
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/docs/operations/{SME_SQUAD_DESIGN,TWO_PLATOON_SPLIT_DESIGN}.md` — 7-domain SME routing + platoon lane split.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `fleet.template` (or pack) renders a complete per-repo fleet: roles, SMEs, run-state, routing, and FinOps ceilings.
- Each repo/module gets its own fleet instance with the repo's own SME set, isolated from every other repo's fleet.
- The template is parameterized (repo id, domains, model tiers, budget), not hand-edited per instance.
- Fleet composition is declared data, validated by a schema, and gate-checked for drift (no false-green).

## Definition of done

- Template renders a working fleet for at least one pilot repo.
- Fleet schema + drift gate pass `make verify`.
- Per-repo isolation demonstrated (two repos' fleets share no state).

items.title: Cannibalize mature agent-profile / SME / persona code into the registry
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
Parent: #144

## Summary

Cannibalize the org's mature agent-profile / SME / persona code into the `agent-orchestrator` registry. The platform schemas already exist (`registry/personas/persona-card.schema.json`, `registry/profiles/agent-profile.schema.json`, `registry/packs/agent-pack.schema.json`); this issue backfills them with content and vocabulary from the best in-org sources.

## Cannibalization sources (verified file paths)

- `kushin77/leaderboard/lib/fleet-roster.sh` — ROLE/TIER/MODEL/TRANSPORT/EFFORT separation + `role_capabilities()` measured per-model JSON (strengths/weaknesses/cost, auditor DISCRIMINATES evidence).
- `kushin77/leaderboard/docker/worker-fleet/personas.yaml` — 15 container personas (role/description/env/memory_file/cron_lines).
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/.claude/agents/{gcp-gatekeeper-sme,ltc-brain-fleet-sre,qa-playwright-sme}.md` — mature SME cards (frontmatter: name/description/tools/model:inherit + Mission/Constraints/Approach/Output-Format).
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/scripts/agent/sme/*.txt` (10 prompts) + `sme-dispatch.sh` — DOMAIN→SME system-prompt library.
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting/infra/docker/worker-fleet/personas.yaml` + `fleet-roster.conf` — ~30 personas + tri-state run-state (required/parked/unverified).
- `kushin77/CMR/docs/SME-PROFILES.md`, `CMR/catalog/sme-registry.tsv` (weekly_spend_ceiling), `CMR/onboarding/agent-profiles/role.schema.json` + `persona-registry.json` + `profiles/*.json`.
- `kushin77/deepseek/config/capabilities.toml` + `docs/operations/sme-card-template.md` + `scripts/sme-card-check.py` — declared-data capability catalog + SME-card shape enforcement.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every harvested asset records source provenance (repo, path, license) in the cannibalization index (GR-10).
- `agent-profile.schema.json` / `persona-card.schema.json` vocabularies are backfilled from CMR's role schema + leaderboard's fleet-roster.

## Definition of done

- Profiles/cards seeded from all listed sources with provenance.
- `make verify` green (registry schemas + catalog parity pass).
- Cannibalization index lists every source path.

## Harvest map — cannibalize-first (owner directive, 2026-09-13)

The mature prior art in `kushin77/leaderboard` and `kushin77/capital-underwriting`
is the source for this issue, not inspiration. Every implementing agent reads
these paths before writing anything:

| Source (repo-relative) | Asset | Verdict | Feeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| leaderboard/lib/fleet-roster.sh | ROLE/TIER/MODEL/TRANSPORT/EFFORT roster | PATTERN | fleet contract + dispatcher |
| leaderboard/docs/LEADERBOARD_PROTOCOL.md | coordination protocol | REFERENCE | #163 dispatcher |
| leaderboard/scripts/cto/cto-orchestrator.sh | CTO overlay orchestration | PATTERN | #163 / #166 |
| leaderboard/docs/CTO_OVERLAY.md + .cto/*.yaml | per-repo governance overlay | PATTERN | #147 / #166 |
| leaderboard/docker/worker-fleet/personas.yaml | fleet personas | READY | registry/personas |
| capital-underwriting/config/leaderboard/capability-registry.json | dispatch routing | PATTERN | #163 |
| capital-underwriting/config/leaderboard/tier-policy.json + route-policy.json | FinOps tier/route policy | PATTERN | #164 |
| capital-underwriting/.claude/agents/*.md + scripts/agent/sme/*.txt | SME cards | REFERENCE | registry/personas + roles |
| capital-underwriting/docs/wiki/ELITE_*.md | commander/general/platoon charters | REFERENCE | #161 / #165 |

verdict (GR-10 provenance); (2) reuse the mature vocabulary — do not invent a
parallel taxonomy; (3) where the mature shape is bash/GitHub-bound, take the
PATTERN and re-implement for this repo, saying so in the PR.

items.title: EPIC: Per-Repo Agent Fleet — Personal CTO Engineering Team with Enterprise Roll-up
items.milestone: M25 - Per-Repo Agent Fleet & CTO Overlay
items.body:
## Concept review (requested)

Reviewed the two named repos plus the org-wide agent-profiling surface. Findings:

- `kushin77/leaderboard` is the fleet coordination + orchestration hub: the **leaderboard concept** (per-session self-registration + a deterministic reporter that computes STALE / CLAIM-MISMATCH / WASTED-EFFORT / N-1-ready, never narrates), the **CTO overlay** (a drop-in `.cto/` directory giving any repo a 4-layer governance team — Executive / Engineering / DevOps / Support — with a JSON Schema and tiered severity), the **role→model roster** (`lib/fleet-roster.sh` — separates ROLE / TIER / MODEL / TRANSPORT / EFFORT and carries measured per-model capability JSON), 15 container `personas.yaml`, 7 `platoons.yaml` lenses, and the Commander / Platoon-Leader / Soldier doctrine.
- `kushin77/capital-underwriting` embeds a production autonomous agent fleet ("the product builds itself"): 3 mature Claude SME cards (`.claude/agents/*.md`), 10 SME system prompts (`scripts/agent/sme/*.txt` + `sme-dispatch.sh`), ~30 fleet personas (`infra/docker/worker-fleet/personas.yaml` + `fleet-roster.conf` run-state), the **capability-registry / route-policy / tier-policy JSON trio** (agent roles + worker fleets + FinOps routing), and the **ELITE charters** (Commander / Lieutenant-Commander / General / Platoon-Leader / Auditor / Scribe) — the "personal CTO engineering team" concept in mature prose. Its `capability{Manifest,Registry,Vocabulary}.ts` is elite-grade schema discipline (tri-state availability + evidence tiers presence/parse/exercised).
- Canonical owners today: `CMR` owns the persona spec + role registry (`docs/SME-PROFILES.md`, `catalog/sme-registry.tsv` with `weekly_spend_ceiling`, `onboarding/agent-profiles/role.schema.json`); `agent-orchestrator` already owns the platform schemas (`persona-card.schema.json`, `agent-profile.schema.json`, `agent-pack.schema.json`).

The requested concept — **each repo/module gets its own agent fleet (SME-focused profiles), acting as its personal CTO engineering team, rolled up to the enterprise/org/GDC, with the group controlling/locking/implementing end-to-end issues to full closure under full admin rights and strict repo separation** — is validated by existing in-org machinery. No new concept must be invented; it must be cannibalized, generalized, templated, and rolled up. The gaps are: (a) no single schema family combines all five layers, (b) the CTO overlay is only partially implemented, (c) no enterprise/GDC roll-up view exists, (d) repo-separation + admin-rights + full-closure controls are spread across charters rather than enforced.

## Scope

- Cannibalize the mature agent-profile / SME / persona / fleet / leaderboard / CTO-overlay assets identified above into `agent-orchestrator` (the agent-orchestration control plane), with GR-10 provenance for every harvested asset.
- Generalize them into a per-repo agent-fleet template/pattern, so any repo/module can instantiate its own SME-focused fleet ("personal CTO engineering team").
- Provide the CTO-overlay drop-in governance layer per repo.
- Provide the leaderboard coordination protocol as the engine state machine.
- Provide enterprise/GDC roll-up: tenant hierarchy + org-level aggregate view.
- Enforce repo separation, admin rights, and end-to-end issue closure under full admin authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every cannibalized asset records its source (repo, path, license) in the cannibalization index.
- A single schema family (persona-card / agent-profile / agent-pack) is the canonical home, backfilled from CMR + leaderboard + capital-underwriting content.
- A repo/module can instantiate a per-repo agent fleet from a template without hand-writing profiles.
- The CTO overlay runs as an honest 4-layer gate (blocking layers genuinely block; no false-green).
- The leaderboard protocol is realized in the engine state machine (self-registration + computed status).
- Enterprise/GDC roll-up shows per-repo fleets aggregated at the org level with FinOps ceilings.
- Repo separation is enforced: no two repo fleets share state; admin rights are scoped per repo with an enterprise-level controller.

## Definition of done

- All child issues below closed with verification evidence.
- `make verify` green with actual output.
- Cannibalization index updated with every harvested source path.
- Provenance recorded (GR-10) for every ported asset.

items.title: Establish the governance board and enforcement gate for CMR/GDC knowledge compliance
items.milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
items.body:
## Summary

Create the decision-making and enforcement structure that governs the knowledge-indexing program, ensures rule adherence, and blocks non-compliant work from proceeding. The governance board owns approvals, exceptions, and remediation escalation; the enforcement gate ensures CMR standards are not optional.

## Scope

- Define board responsibilities, cadence, quorum, escalation paths, and exception handling.
- Specify the enforcement gate as an honest, fail-on-violation control that cannot silently pass.
- Require all rules in the CMR policy set to be measurable, traceable, and reviewable.
- Tie gate output to issue closure, PR merge, and high-risk program decisions.
- Route repeated or severe violations to governance escalation and board review.
- Maintain a clear pattern for approved exceptions and their timeboxes.

## Acceptance criteria

- A governance board charter exists with roles, cadence, and escalation criteria.
- An enforcement gate is implemented and integrated into the standard verification workflow.
- The gate fails when required knowledge, RCA, lessons, provenance, or class conformance is missing.
- No false-green or vacuous pass states are permitted.
- Board review is required for exceptions, repeated violations, and unresolved high-severity drift.
- Compliance and non-compliance are visible through board reporting and issue-driven workflows.

## Definition of done

- Governance board, decision process, and enforcement gate documented and active.
- A representative board review recorded with compliance evidence and follow-up actions.
- Verified gate output demonstrates both red and green states for controlled scenarios.
- Remediation and escalation flows linked to actual issues and board reports.

## Chain

Parent: #138
Blocked-by: #142

items.title: Automatically generate violator remediation issues from policy drift and non-compliance
items.milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
items.body:
## Summary

Develop an automated policy-detection and remediation workflow that creates GitHub issues for violations of CMR rules, quality classes, enforcement gates, RCA expectations, or required governance actions, so drift becomes explicit work instead of invisible backlog.

## Scope

- Detect policy violations including missing RCA, missing lessons, nonconformant class usage, missing provenance, secret exposure patterns, and invalid governance states.
- Build issue-generation logic that creates remediation work using standard templates and required metadata.
- Classify each generated issue by severity, affected repo, owning lane, required SLA, and policy reference.
- Route generated issues to the correct project board, lane owner, or governance queue.
- Prevent repeated violations by including the exact rule, evidence, and corrective steps.

## Acceptance criteria

- A violation scanner runs automatically on changes and on scheduled audits.
- Each detected violation creates a remediation issue with title, labels, summary, owner lane, and corrective steps.
- Generated issues reference the violated CMR rule or policy and include evidence.
- The workflow suppresses duplicates and merges repeated findings into an actionable issue.
- The issue generator works for both repo-level and org-wide compliance gaps.
- Generated issues can be escalated to the governance board when SLA or severity thresholds are breached.

## Definition of done

- Remediation issue generator implemented and tested with representative violations.
- A real output sample captured showing generated issue content and metadata.
- Verification confirms a newly introduced policy violation creates a valid remediation issue.
- Generated issues visible in the board workflow and actionable by the owning lane.
- Evidence from automated tests and gate output included in the closing PR.

## Chain

Parent: #138
Blocked-by: #140

items.title: Enforce RCA and lessons capture for all failures, incidents, and corrective actions
items.milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
items.body:
## Summary

Create a mandatory RCA and lessons lifecycle so every failure, breach, defect, operational incident, or preventable drift is analyzed and recorded using the canonical CMR process, closing the gap between event detection and durable organizational learning.

## Scope

- Require an RCA for all high-priority issues, operational failures, security events, and policy violations.
- Standardize on the canonical RCA template and require traceability to affected work/products.
- Maintain a single lessons ledger as the authoritative record for learnings and corrective actions.
- Require each corrective action to be reflected in the lessons record and mapped back to the underlying driver.
- Detect gaps where incidents occurred without RCA or lessons entries.
- Enforce the "lessons before closure" principle for incident-related work.

## Acceptance criteria

- An RCA template and lessons ledger process are defined and applied consistently.
- Every incident or policy failure has a matching RCA artifact.
- Every RCA links to the originating issue or event and resulting corrective action.
- Every corrective action is recorded in the canonical lessons ledger.
- Missing RCA or lessons entries are detected as failures in the governance gate.
- Violations create actionable remediation follow-ups rather than being silently ignored.

## Definition of done

- RCA and lessons enforcement wired into the project workflow and compliance gate.
- The canonical ledger documents at least one closed incident with linked corrective action.
- Verification confirms noncompliant historical records are identified and remediation issues created.
- Documentation explains escalation, ownership, and review cadence.
- Actual green evidence from the enforcement gate included with the closing PR.

## Chain

Parent: #138

items.title: Enforce CMR class, pattern, and template conformance across repos
items.milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
items.body:
## Summary

Implement an enforceable quality and pattern model that aligns all work to CMR's class-based ladder: template → class → pattern → enterprise → faang → elite, with the iac mandate applying across every layer. Every issue, design artifact, and implementation must be classified and validated against the required standard before merge or closure.

## Scope

- Define and publish the allowed classes and quality expectations for repo work.
- Require issue briefs and implementation outputs to specify class, pattern, and template alignment.
- Validate that work products meet the required standard before PR merge and before closeout.
- Detect non-conformant work from repositories, generated artifacts, or ad hoc design patterns.
- Enforce model tier, lane ownership, compliance, and quality-grade expectations.
- Require explicit mapping of work to canonical CMR standards and any repo-local deviations.

## Acceptance criteria

- A repo-level policy exists that enumerates CMR classes, patterns, and template requirements.
- Every new issue or change set includes the required classification metadata.
- A conformance checker identifies mismatches between declared class and actual implementation quality.
- Violations result in a clear failure in the verification or merge gate.
- Non-conformant work cannot advance without documented corrective action.
- The policy is consistent with the CMR hierarchy and does not create false-green checks.

## Definition of done

- Conformance checks integrated with the verification path and fail on violations.
- Implementation documented and applied to at least one canonical repository workflow.
- A report generated showing pass/fail status for a representative set of repos or issue types.
- Evidence of actual green verification recorded alongside closure.
- Outstanding deviations resolved or explicitly assigned to follow-up remediation issues.

## Chain

Parent: #138
Blocked-by: #139

items.title: Implement the CMR/GDC institutional knowledge indexer
items.milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
items.body:
## Summary

Build the authoritative institutional knowledge index for the CMR/GDC program so repositories, standards, lessons, RCA records, ADRs, and operating guidance are discoverable, versioned, and auditable. The index must reflect the canonical CMR rule hierarchy and make compliance state queryable by engineering and governance teams.

## Scope

- Define the canonical knowledge schema for repositories, standards, patterns, lessons, RCA records, ADRs, and enforcement states.
- Index all authoritative CMR/GDC sources, including rules, execution plans, governance docs, lessons, and issue metadata.
- Capture provenance for every material asset, including origin repo, path, date, owner, and change history.
- Expose a search and query interface that supports program-level discovery and compliance checks.
- Ensure content is generated from source-of-truth artifacts, not hand-maintained mirrors.
- Enforce no secret or sensitive material in indexed artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria

- An indexer exists and runs on a schedule and on-demand.
- Every indexed object includes metadata for source, owner, version, timestamp, and provenance.
- The index covers at minimum: policy docs, golden rules, governance docs, architecture docs, lessons, RCA records, issue metadata, and pattern/template definitions.
- The indexer rejects or flags sources that violate secret policy, provenance requirements, or content integrity rules.
- Query results return source-backed evidence and compliance context.
- The system works from canonical CMR standards and does not rely on duplicated knowledge stores.
- The indexer emits machine-readable output suitable for board reporting and enforcement gating.

## Definition of done

- Implementation merged with a PR closing this issue.
- Indexer runs successfully in a verified environment and outputs a valid catalog.
- Verification includes `make verify` with actual passing output recorded.
- Source provenance present for all material assets indexed.
- Documentation included for usage, maintenance, and refresh cadence.

## Chain

Parent: #138

items.title: EPIC-XX: CMR/GDC Enterprise Knowledge Indexing & Cross-Reference Spine
items.milestone: M24 - Enterprise Knowledge Index & Policy Normalization
items.body:
## Summary

Establish the enterprise-wide knowledge index and cross-reference layer for the CMR/GDC operating model so that code, documentation, issues, PRs, modules, lessons, RCAs, and governance records are discoverable, traceable, and auditable across the full enterprise surface.

This epic is the parent initiative for the aligned CMR/GDC knowledge architecture. It operationalizes the doctrine in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [docs/GOVERNANCE.md](docs/GOVERNANCE.md), [docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md](docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md), and the canonical CMR standards in [vendor/CMR/docs/SOLUTION-CLASSES.md](vendor/CMR/docs/SOLUTION-CLASSES.md), [vendor/CMR/docs/RCA-TEMPLATE.md](vendor/CMR/docs/RCA-TEMPLATE.md), [vendor/CMR/docs/CROSS-REFERENCE-LAYER.md](vendor/CMR/docs/CROSS-REFERENCE-LAYER.md), and [vendor/CMR/board/MILESTONES.md](vendor/CMR/board/MILESTONES.md). The result is a GitHub-native encyclopedia of governed enterprise knowledge, not a repo-local artifact or an optional doc dump.

This is a cross-repo, cross-team effort with enterprise-grade requirements: provenance, no false-green validation, typed relationships, issue-first governance, PR-gated merge discipline, and explicit blast-radius traceability.

## Scope

- Entity indexing across repositories, modules, docs, issues, PRs, comments, commits, release artifacts, runbooks, and decisions
- Typed cross-references between all governed entities using a fixed relationship vocabulary
- Canonical issue/PR/commit provenance and traceability from source to delivery
- Knowledge graph coverage for lessons learned, RCAs, architecture decisions, and operational runbooks
- Module and catalog relationship mapping for load-bearing enterprise surfaces
- Discoverability and navigation of governance state in GitHub-native tools
- Search, impact analysis, and blast-radius tracing for policy, security, and platform changes
- Enterprise operator workflows for adoption, onboarding, and governance review
- Security and compliance constraints: no secrets, no silent failures, no non-provenance assets, no dead links, no false-green gates

## Enterprise workstreams

1. Knowledge graph foundation
2. GitHub-native cross-reference layer
3. Provenance and trust
4. RCA and lessons loop
5. Enterprise discovery and operations
6. Adoption and governance

## Target class and operating posture

- Target class: pattern → enterprise → elite
- Required governance rigor: enterprise-wide, multi-repo, multi-team, audit-grade
- Model tier: MED/HIGH implementation; HIGH/MAX architecture review + adversarial validation
- IaC mandate: all live infrastructure and automation must be declared, not clicked

## Acceptance criteria

- A single, maintained enterprise knowledge graph exists for CMR/GDC with typed edges between core entities
- All governed entities carry the required provenance and cross-reference markers
- Malformed or missing metadata is a conformance failure, never a silent skip
- RCA objects are first-class nodes with caused-by and mitigates relationships
- Cross-reference generation is deterministic, reproducible, and reviewable
- Secret scanning, provenance checks, and dead-link checks are part of the verification path
- The enterprise index is discoverable and usable by platform, security, operations, and PMO
- A clear parent epic and subordinate child issues are defined for each workstream and repo lane
- All work is tracked on the board before implementation and closed with evidence

## Definition of done

- Enterprise knowledge index and cross-reference layer implemented for the controlled CMR/GDC surface
- Typed relationships in place across issues, PRs, docs, code, modules, decision records, and RCAs
- `cmr-refs` marker convention enforced and validated
- Every child issue closed with evidence and linked back to the parent
- Verification gate green with actual output recorded
- No secrets in code, config, or docs; provenance complete
- Documentation and runbooks reflect the agreed enterprise model
- Board kept current; no work orphaned; no issue closed without evidence

## Governance requirements

Issue-first; one issue = one lane = one branch; PR-gated master; verify before done; no false-green gates; no secrets; provenance on all harvested assets; local-code-first; no silent failures; board mandate; FinOps dispatch at lowest capable tier; enterprise scope only.

## Required verification model

- `make verify` passes with real output
- Cross-reference dry-run checks pass
- Conformance checks for `cmr-refs` markers pass
- Secrets scan passes
- No dead links or broken references introduced

items.body:
## Objective
Close the loop between the factual KB, the shared-frontend web UI, and the actual agent execution surfaces so the ecosystem is visible, governable, and cost-aware.

## Scope
- unify indexing health, portal visibility, and workstream traceability in one operator story
- ensure the UI reflects the same truth as the code index and module health gate
- enable E2E controls so operators can see all work, module status, and runtime health from one place

## Acceptance criteria
- the fact-accurate code index and the shared-frontend web UI share the same runtime truth
- module health is visible in the UI and can be audited from a single surface
- no work is considered complete without verification evidence and read-back checks
- the resulting UI supports E2E operator visibility across the ecosystem

## Verify
```bash
make verify
pytest -q e2e/tests/test_golden_path.py e2e/tests/test_negative_controls.py
```

items.title: Module health gate: code-indexing + shared-frontend must be running and verified
items.milestone: KB + Module Health
items.body:
## Objective
Create a production-grade module health gate that proves every CMR module, especially `code-indexing` and `shared-frontend`, is healthy, registered, and ready for use.

## Scope
- mandatory module health checks for all CMR modules
- health/read-back validation before a module is treated as implemented or deployed
- consistent gate semantics across repo, vendor, and portal surfaces
- prevent stale modules from silently passing in the catalog or portal

## Requirements
- each module declares a real verification command and health readout
- a module is not "green" unless the gate genuinely runs and passes
- drift, stale catalog entries, and missing consumer assets fail the gate
- read-back checks must confirm the actual deployed state matches the manifest

## Acceptance criteria
- mandatory modules are checkable via a common gate and report real status
- `code-indexing` and `shared-frontend` are both included in the mandatory health set
- stale or missing runtime states fail loudly and correctly
- CMR issue closure includes the actual gate output

## Verify
```bash
make verify
```

items.title: Deploy shared-frontend at ai.purebliss.app as the agent ecosystem web UI

items.body:
## Objective
Deploy the shared-frontend as the visible, usable web UI for the full agent ecosystem at `https://ai.purebliss.app` and ensure the surface is a compliant CMR module.

## Scope
- serve the shared-frontend shell as the canonical agent ecosystem web UI
- expose all active agent modules, workstreams, health, and E2E controls in a single surfaced dashboard
- align the deployment with the `shared-frontend` mandatory module contract and app-shell standards
- keep the deployment route consistent with the CMR portal model and ecosystem visibility requirements

## Requirements
- route to `ai.purebliss.app` or the canonical hosted equivalent for the web UI
- UI must show the agent registry, module health, active workstreams, and verification surfaces
- shared-frontend must conform to `shared-frontend` module manifest and token design system
- deployment must be auditable and tied to the verification gate
- no manual hidden state; all runtime config must be in declared env vars / secret-manager patterns

## Acceptance criteria
- `shared-frontend` deploys with a visible single-chrome control-plane shell and module routing
- the UI can surface the full agent ecosystem and current work, not a dead home page
- the deployment uses the CMR shared-frontend contract and design tokens
- health/read-back checks are part of the deploy verification
- issue closure includes the actual verification output and deploy evidence

## Verify
```bash
make verify
python3 -m pytest -q e2e/tests/test_golden_path.py e2e/tests/test_negative_controls.py
```

items.title: EPIC: Fact-accurate code-indexing KB + module health for all CMR modules
items.milestone: KB + Module Health
items.body:
## Objective
Make the factual code index the org-wide source of truth for all CMR-managed repos and stop token waste caused by unindexed or stale KB surfaces.

## Scope
- measure and harden all mandatory CMR modules, with `code-indexing` as the first-class runtime KB
- ensure the index is fresh, compiler-accurate, and queryable via MCP/CLI/web surfaces
- tie indexing health to module verification and package publishing gates
- prove the KB reduces unnecessary LLM token spend by eliminating repeated repo scans and stale context

## Requirements
- code-indexing must be treated as a mandatory runtime service, not a fallback convenience
- the index must be fresh, deterministic, and read-back validated before deployment is considered green
- each CMR repo must declare the KB dependency and version in its module manifest
- every change that affects the KB or module health must include a verify command and evidence
- health signals must be visible in the shared UI and in the control-plane views

## Acceptance criteria
- `code-indexing` is present, healthy, and pinned as a mandatory consumer asset for governed repos
- fresh index generation and read-back checks pass on real repos, not mock fixtures
- stale or missing index state fails the gate with a real non-zero result
- module health is documented and visible in the control plane + unified UI
- verification evidence is attached to the issue and linked to the repo gate

## Verify
```bash
make verify
pytest -q e2e/tests/test_golden_path.py e2e/tests/test_negative_controls.py
```

- policy checks prevent unsafe or unauthorized cross-agent execution
- security posture is documented and testable for pilot use

## Acceptance criteria
- multi-agent runs have durable state and explicit task records
- artifacts can be attached and returned across agent boundaries
- cancellations, retries, and escalation paths are measurable and traceable

The module already has registry, gateway, execution-engine, guardrails, identity, telemetry, and control-plane scaffolding, but it does not yet define or implement the protocol, discovery, trust model, or operational rollout required for peer-to-peer agent collaboration.

- observability, auditing, and FinOps attribution

items.title: Sandboxed agent tool execution (Docker/Firecracker isolation + per-category security profiles)
items.body:
## Goal
Add an agent tool-execution sandbox to the guardrails pillar: every tool call an agent makes (file/exec/network/db/cloud/git/docker/k8s) runs in an isolated, resource-capped container (Docker) or microVM (Firecracker) selected from per-category security profiles. Do NOT implement now - this is a backlog feature sourced from a spike find.

## Source (spike #48 find, elevatediq monorepo - read-only verified 2026-09-08)
- `kushin77/elevatedIQ:services/ai-chatbot-orchestrator/internal/sandbox/profiles.go` - 3 security profiles (restricted/standard/privileged: read-only rootfs, no-new-privs, cap-drop, network none/bridge/host, user, CPU/mem/PID quotas, timeout) + `CategoryProfiles` map binding tool categories (file/exec/network/db/cloud/git/docker/k8s) to a profile (fail-closed to restricted).
- `kushin77/elevatedIQ:services/ai-chatbot-orchestrator/internal/sandbox/docker.go` + `internal/firecracker/*` (client.go, vm.go, network.go, snapshot.go) - Docker isolation and Firecracker-go-sdk microVM lifecycle.

## Why adopt (not represented in backlog)
Backlog guardrails issues cover DLP/egress (#27), policy gates (#26), guard honesty (#28), tenant isolation (#30) - but none isolates agent tool execution in a sandbox. A commercial-agent control plane needs this for multi-tenant safety. Not covered by CMR/leaderboard harvests (their execution guards are bash-process-level).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Declare tool categories -> security-profile contract (schema)
- [ ] Docker sandbox executor with per-category profile defaults (fail-closed)
- [ ] Optional Firecracker microVM executor (flag-gated OFF per IaC doctrine)
- [ ] Wire into MCP tool gateway (#20) so tool Execute routes through sandbox + audit
- [ ] Negative tests: restricted profile blocks network/cap-escalation; no-false-green

## Notes
- Harvested asset: harvested_from: kushin77/elevatedIQ@develop services/ai-chatbot-orchestrator/internal/sandbox + internal/firecracker, harvest date 2026-09-08, verdict PATTERN (profiles + category map near-READY; microVM executor is reference).

## EPIC-00 — AI Agent Orchestration SaaS (E2E blueprint)

Closes the design brief captured in #3 (the "Orchestrator" transcript). This epic is the index for the full E2E backlog; every later issue is a child of this plan. Do not close until all child issues are closed and the product is live behind a flag.

**Product**: Multi-tenant SaaS control plane that **organizes, governs, and manages commercial AI agents** (Claude, DeepSeek, Copilot, Gemini, local Ollama, etc.) for enterprises:
- Tenant defines its **agent org**: roles, SME personas, capabilities, boundaries.
- Platform owns agent **identity, profiles, model routing/gateways, guardrails/DLP, budgets/FinOps, memory, execution state, audit, observability**.
- Consumers integrate via **REST API + SDK + MCP**; admins use a **control-plane portal**.

**Canonical architecture (from #3) — five pillars:**
1. **Agent Registry & Profiling** — declarative schemas for system prompts/tools/constraints (phase 1)
2. **Model Gateways** — decoupled multi-provider proxy/router (phase 2)
3. **State-machine execution** — orchestration engine, durable (phase 3)
4. **Security & guardrails** — DLP filters, prompt-injection defense, policy gates (phase 4)
5. **Observability** — full-trace token/latency, FinOps metering (phase 5)
Plus cross-cutting **tenant identity/RBAC (phase 6)**, **control-plane/portal (phase 7)**, and **autonomous ops/governance (phase 8)**.

**Rollout doctrine (adopted from fleet):** every new surface ships **flag-gated OFF** by default (IaC mandate, CMR GR-28); no-false-green gates (leaderboard doctrine); independent verification before merge (CMR GR-12/ADR-0020/0021).

**Source-of-truth plan doc**: build and maintain `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` + `docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md` + `docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md` (index of harvested assets) in this repo.

**Definition of done**: all phases closed; multi-provider agent org can be provisioned by a new tenant end-to-end (signup → org → personas → agents → routed model calls → audit + usage billing) entirely agent-built and flag-gated.

items.body:
So building a lot of different applications and repos and using agents to do so. And building my CMR, you could probably see that from previous chats. So, um, building on that, um, agent profiling, uh, has been very important. So how do you see that in, in a large repo or large count where we're, um, using a lot of profiling, subject matter experts and, uh, that type of, uh, behavior internally, controlling, governing the actual Claude and DeepSeek, uh, agents?

To effectively govern multiple specialized agents, you'll want to implement a hierarchical role-based architecture. This involves defining specific profiles for each agent that dictate their scope of expertise and operating boundaries. Governance is maintained through strict prompt orchestration and context limits to prevent agents from diverging from their assigned tasks or accessing unauthorized data.

So what's the best architecture for this? As my CMR grows, is this its own submodule? Is it a submodule of the organization or either rather just a module or an integration? What's the right way to deal with this? Um so that um I I get it right from the beginning.

The best approach is to structure the CRM as an independent integration connected via API. This decouples the AI logic from your core platform, allowing you to scale agents independently, swap models like Claude or DeepSeek without disrupting the system, and maintain flexibility as requirements grow.

This can happen natively within GitHub.

You can achieve this by managing the CRM integration as a separate repository or a GitHub App. This setup allows you to use GitHub Actions—

So yes, so I have the CMR as a separate repository app. But again, you're you're getting off topic. My focus is specifically the AI agents. And how they run and operate. And how I want them to run and operate. Is that a completely separate repo? And if so, how is this treated in in um elite uh Fang and SAS companies?

Elite SaaS companies manage AI agents in dedicated, centralized repositories separate from the main application. The agents run as independent microservices using orchestration frameworks to handle task routing, context boundaries, and secure model integration. This ensures stable scaling and precise control over how models like yours operate without affecting the core codebase.

Give me the proper name for this repo in the proper SAS.

Companies typically name these repositories using a clear, functional convention. Common names include "ai-agents," "agent-platform," or "orchestration-service" to reflect their purpose within the larger ecosystem. Would you like to explore specific orchestration frameworks for this service?

I like orchestration services or AI orchestration services. Now, what does that mean? Give me a full detail of what this entails.

An AI orchestration service manages the lifecycle, interactions, and routing of multiple AI agents within a larger system. It acts as a central brain that accepts a request, determines which agent is best suited to handle it, provides that agent with the necessary context, securely calls the underlying models like Claude or DeepSeek, and then aggregates the results back to the main application. It also handles things like load balancing, monitoring performance, and enforcing security protocols across the entire cluster.

Give me a full scale end-to-end IT roadmap elite enterprise SaaS scale.

Building an elite enterprise SaaS architecture requires a phased roadmap starting with foundational Infrastructure as Code and CI CD automation. You'll move into a containerized—

star star pause um let me reiterate that I want to give me a full scale end to end IT roadmap lead enterprise SAS SAS scale specifically for our AI agent orchestration repo

An enterprise-grade orchestration service is structured as an independent control plane rather than just another application dependency. This repository houses the agent runtime, a prompt and profile registry, state machine execution, and the strict governance boundaries needed to govern models like Claude and DeepSeek.

Repository structure is the foundation. You'll want directories specifically for reusable CI/CD workflows, custom linters for prompt schemas, and Terraform or Kubernetes manifests for deployment.

The core of the system relies on five main technical pillars. Agent Registry and Profiling uses declarative YAML schemes to define system prompts, tools, and constraints. Model Gateways act as a decoupled proxy for routing requests between different models.

State Machine execution uses an orchestration engine to maintain state across multi-step execution loops. Security and guardrails handle Data Loss Prevention filters and prompt injection defense. Finally, observability provides full-trace logging of token counts and latency.

To achieve elite SaaS scale, follow a four-stage roadmap. First, build the profile engine and Gateway client layer. Second, deploy and stateful execution engine like Temporal.

Third, roll out enterprise guardrails like real-time DLP to strip credentials before they hit public APIs. Finally, configure local model fallbacks to maintain high availability.

### Email (copy-paste)

Subject: Invitation: 30–45m pilot — Investigation Canvas (help improve RCA workflow)

Hi {name},

We're running a short pilot to validate an Investigation Canvas prototype that helps engineers perform root cause analysis more quickly and collaboratively. Would you join a 30–45 minute guided session to try it and provide feedback?

What we'll do:
- 20–25m: Guided walkthrough using a sample investigation (link events, add annotations)
- 10–15m: Debrief and short survey (7 questions)

Available slots (example):
- {slot1}
- {slot2}
- {slot3}

If you're interested, reply with your preferred time(s) or click to add to the calendar: {calendar-link}

Thanks — your feedback will directly shape Phase 2 improvements.

Best,
{organizer name}

---

### Slack (copy-paste)

Hi @{user} — quick ask: would you join a short 30–45m session to pilot a new Investigation Canvas prototype? We'll walk through one scenario and ask you to complete a short survey afterwards.

If yes, please reply with your availability or pick a slot from: {link-to-schedule}

Thanks — should be quick and will directly shape improvements.

(If no response in 48h, follow up with: "Hi {name}, just checking whether you had a chance to review my invite for the Investigation Canvas pilot — any preferred times? Appreciate it.")

---

### Calendar invite (copy-paste)

Title: Investigation Canvas Pilot — 30–45m

When: {date} {start_time} — {end_time}
Where: Video call (Google Meet / Zoom) — {meeting-link}

Agenda:
1. 5m — Intro & goals
2. 20–25m — Guided walkthrough: link events, add annotations
3. 5–10m — Debrief + open feedback
4. 5m — Complete survey: {link-to-PILOT_FEEDBACK_SURVEY.md}

Notes:
- Please join on time; session will be recorded with your permission.
- After session, please complete the short survey so we can aggregate feedback.

---

### Quick RSVP message for replies

Thanks {name} — confirmed for {slot}. I'll send calendar invite shortly.

If you need to reschedule, reply with new preferred times.
